WHAT IS PAID is that a customer auditing this package now sees YamlDotNet. The guards narrow rather than vanish: exactly ONE package reference, NAMED so a swap fails too, and exactly one parser-shaped type, so a second grammar is still the drift the original test was protecting against. The parser's result types sit in Gg.Contracts.Authoring, excluded from the pinned-id and vocabulary rules for the reason Gg.Contracts.Description already is - nothing in either is ever serialized, so a pinned id would be a promise about something that never crosses a boundary - with a staleness check that an excluded namespace holding nothing is an error. AND `gg envelope validate` LEARNS THE ROLE: it reads a document as what its containing directory says it is, and NAMES the role it read. That is ADR-0018 § 7's fourth refusal, the one that gets skipped because the document is not malformed but misplaced - a complete envelope copied from root.yaml into a narrowings directory parses, validates, and would hand a team `scope:` and `constitution:` through a merge nobody gated.

A THIRD KIND OF NAME. RepositoryNarrowingNames composes `<repository>/<filename>` - what a narrowing living in a service repository is called (ADR-0018 § 7). Namespaced, because without it a team shadows a compliance regime by choosing a filename, which is a widening performed by a merge. THE LEFT HALF IS THE REGISTRY KEY AND NOT THE FORGE PATH: a path is a display label that may drift, and a name built from one would rename every narrowing the day somebody renames a repository on the forge. THE LAST SLASH IS THE SEPARATOR, and that single fact is what keeps the mapping injective: a registry key may hold a slash - a slug is a slug - while a document name may not, because it is one file in one directory. Splitting on the FIRST would parse `acme/widgets/pci` as a document called `widgets/pci`, which cannot exist, silently. A COMPOSED NAME CAN NEVER EQUAL AN ESTATE NAME, free by construction and asserted anyway: an estate name is one path component and a composed one always carries a slash, so shadowing is impossible rather than discouraged and `flight` stays reserved without anybody defending it. The halves are held to DIFFERENT rules on purpose - the left is a slug, the right is handed straight to AirspaceNames so `payments/PCI` and `payments/pci` cannot be two names for one regime on a case-insensitive filesystem. And the one the registry lets through is refused here: a repository key may contain `@` because the registry refuses only blank and newlines, but versions are qualified name@vN, so a key carrying one composes to a name nothing can parse a version out of. NameRuleTests' single-decider scan fires on this and rides a written exemption - with a test that PROVES the delegation rather than claiming it, because a second name rule that merely says it defers is the exact drift that scan exists to catch.

ABSENT AND UNREACHABLE ARE TWO ANSWERS. ReasonKinds gains declared-and-absent and forge-unreachable, and the distinction is the whole of ADR-0018 section 6. A declared directory that is not there at the pinned commit is a MISCONFIGURATION - usually a sequencing one, the tap turned on before the team committed anything, or the directory sitting on a branch and not at the commit this flight is working from - and the fix is a merge. A forge that cannot be asked is an OUTAGE, with nothing for the tenant to fix; collapsing the two makes a forge incident look like somebody's mistake and sends the person having the outage to check a declaration that is perfectly correct. NEITHER MEANS THE REPOSITORY CONSTRAINS NOTHING, which is the third answer and the one a read that did not happen must never produce: a fetch that 404s and composes as no narrowing is indistinguishable from a repository that chose to constrain nothing, and that is the silent weakening this feature exists to prevent. Both sentences are asserted not to make that claim - and the assertion was WRONG TWICE before it was right, banning first the word 'unconstrained' and then the phrase 'constrains nothing', in sentences that used both contrastively to say the opposite. A guard that bans a word rather than a meaning fails on the sentence that says the right thing; the sentences now say what IS true rather than naming what they are not, and a liveness twin proves the narrowed check still bites. A HALT IS NOT A REFUSAL, so both belong to the failed family: nothing was refused, the flight was admitted and cannot be evaluated, and filing them under refused would put a flight that is WAITING in the same bucket as a document somebody was told no about. Both join All in the commit that declares them - 0.65.0's lesson for the second slice running, where stale-working-copy shipped with a sentence and no entry, invisible to the fingerprint that reads the list and to the guard whose whole job is noticing a new value.

ACCEPTS: IS THE FLOOR BOTH HALVES OF ADR-0020 COMPUTE FROM, and step 0 found it absent along with the half nobody had noticed: THERE WAS NO SUBJECT-KIND VOCABULARY EITHER. What this codebase called a subject was a repository registry name, and a launch request carries a work kind, an environment and a repository as three unrelated optional strings; `repo` was not a value anywhere, so accepts: had nothing to range over. SubjectKinds is minted closed, with one member, because the value this vocabulary exists to make writable today is the EMPTY LIST - a statement `[]` makes and no amount of optionality does. AN UNKNOWN KIND HALTS rather than reading as no constraint: the permissive reading turns a typo in accepts: into a kind that accepts everything, with nothing on the page saying so. SCOPE STAYS REQUIRED AND GAINS `none` AS A VALUE, never becoming optional, because a line that can be dropped is a constraint that can be dropped silently - evidence: was authorable, load-bearing at the gate, emitted by neither render path, and an edit round trip stripped it. And it is a TIGHTENING: `**` was the only way to write unbounded and was indistinguishable from a bound somebody meant, so after this subjectless work says `none` and `**` goes back to meaning every path. THE AGREEMENT IS REFUSED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and neither refusal is the other's contrapositive: a kind over a tree that bounds no path would fly unbounded over a repository, and a kind with no tree that bounds a path has written a rule nothing can read, which is a gate that reports satisfied by never running. Both name the field, the value and the kind. THE AGREEMENT IS ROLE-FREE AND THE ABSENCE IS NOT, which is why Validate gains a role-aware overload rather than a parameter: carrying accepts: is itself the claim to be a work kind, so the two fields can be checked against each other with no topology in front of them - reachable from a parse of one file, which is what lets validate catch it before an apply happens. Whether a work kind was ALLOWED to omit the field, and whether root was allowed to declare it, are questions about the role the document was applied to, and the role is never read from the document. ABSENT IS REFUSED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED to [repository], even though that is what every kind before this field meant: the default would put a subjectless kind one keystroke from a kind that takes a tree with nothing on the page saying which was meant, and the whole point of section 1 is that `nothing was written` and `nothing is bounded` must not look alike.

NONE MEETS A GLOB, AND ADR-0020 DOES NOT LIST THE QUESTION. Root is not a work kind: it always applies, it always carries a scope, and composition is a meet - so the FIRST flight a tenant opens for a subjectless kind computes `src/**` against `none`, and nothing defined that. It fell through to `neither contains the other`, which is correct for two globs and nonsense for a glob and a declaration that there is nothing to glob over, so section 1 was shipping the failure section 2 exists to prevent. SECTION 2 DOES NOT RESCUE IT: section 2 is about rules reading fact families the kind cannot produce, and the scope FIELD is not a rule and is not read from a fact - it saves the obligations and leaves the field it was written to protect. DECIDED AS A DOMAIN MISMATCH, which is the ruling section 2 already makes one noun over: a path bound is a statement about a tree, work that accepts no subject has no tree, so the floor's bound is not narrowed away and is not in conflict - it does not apply, decided from the documents alone without evaluating a fact. THE COMPUTED VALUE IS THE SAME AS `none absorbs`, and that is recorded rather than glossed: what differs is not the string but that the answer comes from a declaration rather than from a claim about which of two bounds is smaller. The permissive reading is the same bytes and a different argument, and the argument is what the next person reads. AND THE TRAP THE MEET RULE OPENS IS CLOSED IN THE SAME RELEASE, found while writing the test for it: with `none` absorbing, a ROOT that said `scope: none` would bound every path-taking kind in the tenant to nothing - QUIETLY, where before the meet rule it produced a refusal. So `none` is now legal exactly where `accepts: []` is, which also makes the composer's none branch unreachable except by a document that DECLARED it takes no subject: the reasoning is checkable rather than merely stated. THE WIRE SURFACE IS UNCHANGED and this is still a version, because a consumer pins an exact one and composition now answers differently for inputs it already accepted - nine earlier entries share a surface with their predecessor for the same reason.

AN ENVELOPE IS A SUBJECT, AND IT HAS NO TREE. SubjectKinds shipped in 0.78.0 with ONE member and an argument that the value the vocabulary existed to make writable was the empty list. ADR-0020 section 1's table has THREE rows - `[repo]` takes a path glob, `[]` takes `none`, and `[envelope]` takes `none` because THE SUBJECT IS THE BOUND - and I had read the section through a slice note rather than the text. So `none` is not the value for NO SUBJECT: it is the value for NO TREE, and having no subject is one way of having no tree. THE SECOND MEMBER IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: an envelope-change flight is a work kind that already ships, whose subject is a document, and which had no honest declaration available to it - `[]` would have said it is about nothing and `[repository]` would have said it is about a tree. THE RULE IS RE-EXPRESSED RATHER THAN EXTENDED: a path glob is legal exactly when the kind accepts a subject that HAS a tree, so a fourth subject kind costs one classification rather than an edit to a refusal - which is the difference between a vocabulary and a list of special cases. ANY rather than ALL, and the case emptiness could not have answered at all: a kind accepting both a repository and an envelope takes a glob, because something in the set has paths to select from and refusing would leave that half unbounded. HasTree is TOTAL AND THROWS rather than defaulting, for the reason every totality guard in this package exists: a kind nobody classified would fall through to whichever answer the default happened to be, and that answer silently decides what scope its work kinds may write - permissively in one direction and impossibly in the other. A value joining a closed vocabulary is a version by construction: the only safe response to an unknown value is to halt, so every prior reader is broken by design and told so by this number.

A RULE THAT COULD NEVER APPLY SAYS SO, AS A MEMBER RATHER THAN A FOURTH VALUE. ADR-0020 section 2 marks an obligation reading a fact family the work kind cannot produce as inapplicable, decided at authoring and never evaluated - and a decision that leaves no trace is indistinguishable from an omission, which is the failure this vault keeps meeting one surface over. So the answer is STATED: ObligationAttribution.Inapplicable carries the fact family, and gg why renders a `never:` line before the condition. THIS CORRECTS MY OWN DECISION AT SLICE OPEN, made from a slice note rather than the ADR's text. I had recorded that structural inapplicability would take its own fourth plan state, on the grounds that it must not share a word with an evaluated-false does-not-apply. Both sources disagree with me and agree with each other: the ADR says the answer IS does-not-apply, and the note says the slice adds a fourth REASON for a thing to be in that bucket, requiring only that it not share a word with cannot-tell-yet. THE COST SETTLES IT EITHER WAY: a member may be added freely and a value may not, because the only safe response to an unknown value is to halt - so a fourth Attachments value would break every prior reader by design, for a distinction the ADR did not ask for. The attachment stays not-attached, which is true, and the structural reason travels beside it as something no older reader has to understand. IT IS THE FAMILY RATHER THAN A SENTENCE, because Because already carries the words and a caller has to tell `this was measured and did not fire` from `this could never fire` by a null check: the first may fire tomorrow and the second cannot. The value is validated against FactKinds.All, so a reason nobody can check is refused where it is written. AND VALIDATE GAINED ONE ARM, which is the half worth reading twice: a not-attached obligation was required to name a condition, because without one there is no way to tell a false condition from an obligation nobody wrote. Structural inapplicability is precisely the case that HAS no condition - no-file-outside-scope on a subjectless kind applies always, to work that can never answer it - so that rule would have refused the exact answer section 2 exists to give. Inapplicable is what makes it distinguishable now, which is what the rule was protecting.

CHECK-RUN: THE FIRST DESTINATION WHOSE ACT LEAVES THIS SYSTEM, and ADR-0020 section 4's `comment` corrected on evidence. Section 4 names comment, work-item and message and puts all three on ports it says Platform Architecture already designs. NONE OF THEM HAS MACHINERY: there is no notification port in any form - every match for it in the control plane is Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY plumbing - and Intent is a URI stored on a lease and rendered into a prompt that nothing resolves in either direction. What DOES have machinery is the check run: a command, a receptor that returns the event, an adapter, and the one write MetadataOnlyTests permits the client to make. AND THE PERMISSION DECIDES IT. The installation holds `checks` and no write on issues or pull requests, asserted live against the forge, so `comment` costs a re-grant every installation must approve and nobody can un-ask - one slice after fifteen declined that same cost for contents:read. This is also strictly better than the slice's own pre-committed cut, where the act would have been admitted, recorded, and never performed. THREE DESTINATION KINDS ALREADY SHIP AND TWO OF THEM ARE PERFORMED BY ADMISSION ITSELF - envelope-change and airspace-registration both land inside the tenant's own stream and registries - so section 3's `the first outward act performed by admission rather than held by the agent` is right only for acts that LEAVE. pull-request leaves and is performed by the RUNNER on the customer's credential, which section 3 says in as many words. This one leaves AND is performed by the control plane, which is what makes section 3's containment argument true rather than nearly true: the agent that drafted the text never holds a credential that could post it. IT IS NOT A COMMENT WEARING A DIFFERENT NAME. A check run does not thread and carries no approve/reject verdict on a forge object; what it carries is a governed, attributed, durable statement on the commit under review, posted only after admission. When a re-grant is being asked for anyway, comment joins on its own merits. preserve-unadmitted is refused on it by a rule that already generalises to every kind that is not pull-request, so section 5 costs a test rather than a check - and the other half is asserted too, so the refusal reads as being about this kind rather than about the key having been retired.

PRODUCES: THE RELATION ADR-0020 SECTION 2 LOST, AND THE COMPARISON THAT WAS NEVER MADE. ADR-0014's relations table has two rows - work kind to subject kinds accepted, and work kind to fact families produced - and ADR-0020 section 2 derived the second from the first. That cannot separate two kinds that share a subject: `implement` and `review` are both about a repository and do not have the same fact vocabulary, so every family reachable from a repository was judged producible by both. ADR-0021 section 3 restores the lost relation and this version carries it. A work kind declares `produces:`, absent is refused rather than defaulted for the same reason `accepts:` is - the default that suggests itself, everything the subject allows, IS the behaviour being corrected, so it would leave every kind whose author never heard of the field exactly as it was. It composes work-kind-only and EnvelopeNarrowing has no member for it, which is the whole reason it is declared rather than derived from `moves:`: moves compose across layers, so a narrowing living in a customer's own repository could delete every scope gate on its own flights by narrowing moves to [read]. AND THE DEFECT FOUND WHILE ADDING IT: EnvelopeDirection.Widening never compared Accepts. It carried a [Composes] operator from the day it shipped, so it passed the drift guard in the static constructor, and was simply absent from the comparison - a work kind that narrowed `accepts:` computed tighter-or-equal and walked through the gate a floor exists to hold. Both fields now compare by containment: declaring a field that was absent is not a widening, reducing it or withdrawing it is.

THE SURFACE IS UNCHANGED FROM 0.83.0 AND THAT IS THE POINT WORTH RECORDING: what moves is a REFUSAL, not a shape. A work kind may no longer declare `produces:` naming a family measured from a tree while its `accepts:` names no subject that has one - work with no tree claiming to measure one. ADR-0021 section 3's veto, refused where an author can still act rather than discovered by a flight that halts. Built as the same refusal section 1 already ships for `accepts:` against `scope: none`: two fields on one document that have to agree, checked with no role in front of them, naming BOTH halves so a reader knows which of two lines to change. TREES RATHER THAN EMPTINESS - `envelope` is a real subject kind with no tree, so `accepts: [envelope]` is as unable to yield a change manifest as `accepts: []` is. FactCategories moves into this package to make that possible: whether a family needs a tree is a property of the vocabulary, and the vocabulary is declared here, so leaving the classification control-plane-side meant either a second copy of it - two computations of one question, where being wrong removes a gate - or a refusal an author could not get until they applied. It joins the FACT fingerprint rather than this one, so fact-vocabulary moves to 0.17.0: adding a family and classifying it become a single reviewable act. NULL IS SILENCE AND NOT EMPTINESS, which a shipped test caught in the first draft of this arm: a document that never declared `accepts:` has not said it takes no subject, and is owed the role refusal rather than a contradiction it did not state.

ONE FACT, ONE SENTENCE. The surface is unchanged again - what moves is where a sentence is composed. The plan rendered 'this work kind cannot produce X, so this rule can never apply to it' and `gg why` rendered 'this kind of work cannot produce X, so this rule can never apply to it': two paraphrases of one claim, composed independently in two repositories, agreeing today because somebody typed carefully twice. A person reading a plan and a person reading `gg why` are checking the same claim and the only thing they can compare is the words, so two spellings is the manifest hazard wearing a different coat - two computations that agree until the first fix to either. Inapplicability.Because is the one composition, it lives beside the vocabulary it names because both sides already reference here, and it throws on a family the contract does not declare rather than composing a reason nobody can look up. Neither repository is allowed a second copy, asserted by a scan over the sentence's own shape rather than over its words - `cannot produce` alone matches the contradiction refusal and three doc comments, and a control that reports the vocabulary instead of the duplication is one that gets exempted into uselessness.

A third intent kind, and it is the one FlightIntentKinds predicted in writing: "adding a third - an issue, a pull request, a ticket - is a contract change, which is what makes it visible; the FIELD to carry it already exists, which is what makes it cheap." The prediction was half right. The change is visible and the fields did NOT already exist - a work item is a provider and an id, and neither is a URI or a sentence, so `ticket` arrives with two new members beside it. A VALUE in a closed vocabulary rather than only a member, which is why this number moves: the only safe response to an unknown value is to halt, so an added value breaks every prior reader by design, and that is the point of making it visible. THE ID IS DECLARED AND NEVER PARSED. An id that is a URI, or that carries a path, is refused naming the field - because deriving structure from a string somebody typed is the move slice nine retired when it stopped lifting a repository's provider out of an intent URI's host, and it breaks the same way on a vanity host and on a work item moved between projects. The larger version of that is still live and out of scope here: FlightRepos.From reads only a URI's AbsolutePath and the registry matches on that path alone, so a link at any host resolves to whichever registered entry shares its path. Building a second thing shaped like it would have been the cheapest possible mistake. THE PROVIDER IS A FREE STRING and stays one - gg is public and names no forge, and a closed provider vocabulary here is that rule broken one noun over. Which providers actually resolve is the control plane's knowledge and the Intent port's problem, and the port is not in this slice: nothing fetches a work item, nothing reads its text, and the two members are a declaration rather than an address. A ticket is ONE PAYLOAD CARRIED IN TWO FIELDS, which is the only structurally new thing in the validator: the payload count stops being a count of non-empty strings, so a half-filled ticket is diagnosed as a missing FIELD rather than as an intent carrying nothing - the wrong sentence, and one that sends somebody looking in the wrong half of their document. AND THE CONTAINMENT SHIPS IN THE SAME VERSION, because a kind that names a ticket without it would be one keystroke from a gate that reads the ticket. An obligation whose `rule` decides on a work item's text, or whose `when` attaches on it, is refused WHERE IT IS WRITTEN - named specifically on the `obligations.` precedent, and for the same reason: somebody will type it, because reading the ticket is the obvious thing to want, and the generic unknown-rule sentence would read as a version that has not got round to it yet. The refusal deliberately does NOT offer the list of known rules, because offering it invites a search for the one that reads the ticket. A ticket's title, description and comments are a person's typed words: they are `stated` and can never be `measured`, and a gate resting on them is a gate anyone who can comment on the ticket can answer - which is not who the envelope named. It matches on the citation `intent.` and never on the substring, so `intentional-drift` stays an ordinary typo. EnvelopeNarrowing shares the validator, so the smaller door is closed by the same line.

A strategy can declare how many members should be WARM before anything asks. Everything in a strategy was a maximum - inventory.size is how many the pool may hold, bounds.pool-max is how many may be warm at once - and nothing said how many it SHOULD hold, so warming could only ever happen behind a flight that was already waiting. That is the reactive half; slice twelve deferred the other one in writing as its own pre-committed cut ("warming ahead of demand to a time-to-warm target"), and this is the field that makes it expressible. inventory.warm is the first number in a strategy that is not a ceiling, which is to say the only one a decider can be SHORT of. It is a MEMBER and it defaults to ZERO, which is the whole reason this is cheap: a member may be added freely and a value may not, and zero means warm-only-behind-demand, so every strategy already in force reads back and decides exactly as it did. A default of anything else would have turned every applied strategy into a proactive one on the deploy that shipped this. Two refusals, and deliberately not three: warm below zero is refused (below zero is not a smaller kind of zero, it is a number nothing can act on), and warm above bounds.pool-max is refused naming BOTH numbers per Article XI. A warm above inventory.size looks like it deserves its own arm and is UNREACHABLE - pool-max > size is already refused, so anything above the inventory is above the bound first - and shipping an unreachable refusal inside a slice about controls that are never invoked would have been a poor joke. StrategyContainmentTests still holds: int is an allowed shape and 'warm' names no host, endpoint or secret.

A pool member can be given a runner identity of its own. Two routes: a resident runner mints a single-use nonce for one named member (POST /v1/pools/{pool}/members/{member}/credential, runner audience, and 403 is the arm that matters - a member presenting its own token must not mint another), and the member redeems that nonce for a real credential (POST /v1/pools/members/redeem, ANONYMOUS by necessity, because a member has no credential yet; 409 is the second attempt being told it is spent).

Why it exists: nothing has ever run inside a pool member, because nothing could give one an identity. The only mechanism that worked baked a copied developer session.json into an image, which lasts twelve hours and carries the whole developer surface - not something a tenant can operate.

A nonce rather than the credential because GET /containers/gg-pool-*/json is reachable through the scope proxy: anything in a member's environment is readable by an inspect for the life of the container, so what goes in must be worthless once spent.

MemberCredentialIssued carries a runner identity and nothing wider - no session, no principal - because a member runs a customer's code.

A registered repository can declare the ref work starts from, which is the member that makes a flight about a WORK ITEM able to have a repository at all. A ticket intent is a provider and an id: it names no repository and therefore no ref, so such a flight resolved to nothing, its runner materialized an empty tree, and the agent reported - correctly - that there was nothing there to work on. FlightLaunchRequest.Repository has been declared since flights had selections and says WHICH repository a flight is about; what it could never say is at which ref, and FlightRepo.PinnedRef is required. THE REF CANNOT COME FROM THE FLIGHT and it cannot be guessed. Defaulting to refs/heads/main control-plane-side is the exact substitution FlightRepo refuses in writing - 'a uri naming no ref produces no repository rather than a guessed default branch' - and it is wrong on every repository whose trunk is called something else. A person opening a flight about a work item knows the work item, not the branch policy, so pinning from there would be pinning from the least informed place in the system. It belongs on the registration, beside provider, forge id and credential mode: WHO a repository is, which the registrar knows and nobody downstream does. A MEMBER AND OPTIONAL, so every repository registered to date reads back and resolves exactly as it did - absence is not a default branch, it is a repository a ticket flight cannot start work on, and that flight is refused rather than given a branch somebody invented. Nullable on the way OUT as well, unlike credential and like narrowings: an absent credential and a declared 'required' are the same fact so that one resolves, while these two are different facts and the absence has to survive the round trip. FULLY QUALIFIED, REFUSED OTHERWISE. RepositoryRefs.Validate takes shape and deliberately not existence - whether a ref resolves is the forge's answer and a runner's question, and this repository names no forge and reaches none. A bare 'main' is refused where it is written, because a branch and a tag of one name are two different commits and choosing the namespace on the author's behalf is the guess this member exists to remove. Branches, tags and pull refs all pass: a flight already pins refs/pull/n/head on the BASE repository, which is what makes a fork need no credential of its own, and a validator that knew only about branches would break forks.

A lease can name the WORK ITEM a flight is about, and not only a link. This is the member that makes a ticket flight runnable at all: LeaseGranted carried the intent as a URI and nothing else, a ticket is a provider and an id (contract 0.86.0 added the kind and declared both fields ON THE INTENT), and the lease never learned to carry them. The runner invokes on a non-empty intent uri, so EVERY ticket flight since 0.86.0 has been leased, materialized a tree, and returned without invoking anything - no refusal, no fact, no reason. Silent, and the same registered-not-invoked shape as the kind itself: 0.86.0's own note said 'nothing fetches a work item, nothing reads its text, and the two members are a declaration rather than an address', which was true and stayed true one layer down. BESIDE IntentUri RATHER THAN INSTEAD OF IT. A ticket is a provider and an id; a link is a link; and a runner has to be able to tell which of the two it was handed, because what it can do with them differs. Collapsing them into one field would mean composing a URL out of a provider and an id, which this repository cannot do - it names no forge - and which is the derivation slice nine retired when it stopped lifting a repository's provider out of an intent URI's host. It breaks the same way on a vanity host and on a work item moved between projects. THE ID IS DECLARED AND NEVER PARSED, 0.86.0's rule for the same field one layer up, restated here because a lease is read by a runner rather than by a validator and the temptation to read structure out of it is larger. ALL THREE ABSENT IS A REAL STATE, not a half-filled one: a flight about a sentence names no external work, is shipped and is intended, and nothing here should make it look malformed. Both members are optional, so every lease in flight reads back and behaves exactly as it did.

A runner can be registered RESERVED to the person registering it, which is the first thing in this protocol that lets a runner take LESS. Labels only ever say yes: a flight's requirements are matched by JSONB containment against what a runner advertises, and containment is monotone in the runner's labels - adding one can only ever add work. An untargeted flight requires nothing, nothing is contained by every label set including the empty one, and so a laptop running `gg runner up` is a candidate for every untargeted flight in its tenant with no value it can advertise to change that. Measured before it was designed against: two runners on one host, one flight with no selection, and the flight landing on whichever asked first. RESERVED IS NOT A LABEL, and the distinction is load-bearing. A reserved runner may advertise nothing at all and still be reachable by its holder's flights; spelling it as a label would make reserving a laptop require charting an environment first, and would inherit containment's one direction - the thing being fixed. It is a narrowing on the QUEUE rather than a capability claim. A BOOLEAN RATHER THAN A PRINCIPAL. The request says 'reserve this to me' and the control plane is what knows who me is. Reserving somebody else's runner routes work at a person who did not ask for it - a different act, with a different approver, and closer to FlightAwaitingDecision.Approver's category than to attribution's - so it is legitimate and deliberately not this version. A member here that could name a principal would make that act reachable through a request the RUNNER ITSELF composes, which is why the type's shape is asserted rather than only its behaviour: adding one fails a build. AT REGISTRATION, so there is no unreserved window. A runner reserved by a later call takes the tenant's public work until that call lands, which on a busy tenant is every flight in the queue - and the point of reserving a laptop is that untargeted work never lands on it, not that it mostly does not. DEFAULTS TO FALSE, which is what every runner in every deployment does today. A registration written before this member existed means what it meant, and it did not mean reserved. Whether that default is right in the long run is a real question and an open one: the safe direction is a runner that takes only what it was told to take, every existing deployment depends on the opposite, and reversing it later is a breaking change that has to be announced. Recorded as a deferral rather than settled - deciding now that it will never reverse would also be a decision.

A runner's reservation can be set and cleared AFTER it was registered. 0.91.0 put the decision at registration, which is where it has to be for there to be no unreserved window - but registration is a moment and a machine outlives it. Every laptop in every fleet was registered before anybody thought about reservations, and requiring re-registration to change one boolean means destroying a thirty-day credential to do it, on a host where nobody may be signed in. POST and DELETE on one path, both DEVELOPER audience with a session header, and a runner may not reserve, release or read its own. That is not tidiness: the value decides what work this runner is OFFERED, so a runner able to change it could widen its own queue, which is the one thing reserving exists to stop. It is the pool-member rule one noun over - 'the one value that must not be a runner's to choose'. THE REQUEST BODY IS EMPTY AND THAT IS NOT A PLACEHOLDER. The act is 'reserve this to me': the control plane knows who me is from the credential that authenticated the call, and the runner is named by the path. The only member such a body could grow is a principal, and reserving somebody ELSE's runner routes work at a person who did not ask for it - a different act, with a different approver, closer to FlightAwaitingDecision.Approver's category than to attribution's. Leaving the body empty is what keeps that act out of reach rather than one field away. THE RESPONSE NAMES A PERSON BY DISPLAY, NEVER BY ID, which TakeoverHeld.By settled: 'a principal's display, never a name typed in'. 'Somebody else has this' sends a person nowhere and a uuid sends them somewhere worse. 404 RATHER THAN 403 for a runner that is not this tenant's, which is the heartbeat route's rule and its reason: the shape of a refusal must not tell a caller which runner ids exist, because that is enumerating the fleet. 409 on POST for a runner somebody else already holds - taking a reservation from another person is a different act and is not this one. AND DELIBERATELY NO 409 ON DELETE: releasing a runner nobody reserved is the state the caller asked for, not an error, and refusing it would turn 'make sure this is free' into a two-step dance with a race in the middle.

A flight can name the runner it is for, which is the half that makes reserving usable. 0.91.0 and 0.92.0 let a runner say whose work it takes; this lets a person say which machine a piece of work is for. Without it, reserving a laptop means its holder's work lands there and nothing else can be sent there deliberately - a narrowing with only one direction, which is the shape this whole slice exists to stop repeating. THE RUNNER STILL PULLS, and that is worth stating because 'direct a flight at a machine' sounds like the opposite. Push here is a PERSON choosing a machine, not the control plane opening a connection to one: the flight is narrowed by an id, and the runner it names claims it through the same claim path it uses for everything else, on its own schedule. Rule 4 of docs/patterns.md - client-side polling - is untouched, and this is the answer to the push request that was asked for, delivered as targeting. AN ID RATHER THAN A LABEL, deliberately. A label says what a machine CAN DO and several machines may answer to one; direction names ONE machine. Spelling it as a label would make 'this one' unsayable, which is precisely the thing being added - and it would inherit containment's one direction, which is what 0.91.0's note is about. It sits beside Environment and Repository, the two selections a flight already declares: where it runs, what it is about, and which machine. Null inherits, exactly as they do, and here inheriting means 'any runner that may take it' - which is nearly every flight and every flight in the air today. The control plane validates the id against the tenant's own fleet; a flight directed at a runner nobody registered is refused at the door rather than becoming a flight nothing can ever claim.

A runner can be PARKED - withheld from claiming, by a person, without going offline and without giving up the lease in hand. LeaseClaimStates grows a fifth value, which is a closed vocabulary moving and therefore the most consequential change in this slice. PARKED IS ITS OWN STATE RATHER THAN A NARROWED-AWAY FLIGHT, and that is the whole design decision. A parked runner filtered out inside the matcher's WHERE would answer `pending` - the same answer an idle fleet gets - and collapsing those two silences is precisely the defect `waiting` was added to fix: 'an idle fleet and a fleet blocked on something looked identical'. So parking is decided BEFORE the pick and reported as itself. NOT OFFLINE, and not terminal. A parked runner keeps beating; parking withholds claims and does not take the machine away, so one that stopped beating IS offline and takeover must still reclaim its flight. The request is answered and the runner asks again later, exactly as it does for pending. AN OLD RUNNER HALTS ON THIS, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN WORKING. RunnerProtocolClient says so in writing - 'HALT ON A STATE THIS BINARY DOES NOT KNOW. The vocabulary is closed precisely so a fifth value is a version move; guessing would make the closure decorative.' Which makes DEPLOY ORDER load-bearing rather than a detail: ship the binaries first, or refuse old revisions at the door with ProtocolTooOld and GG-Supported-Protocols, and never discover it by parking a runner in production. A RUNNER NEVER REPORTS ITS OWN STATUS, and this does not become the first way it could. Both verbs are a person's, Developer audience with a session header and no runner header anywhere near them: parking withholds work FROM a machine, and a machine able to declare it would be reporting on itself. RunnerStates does NOT grow, and the asymmetry is the point: state is derived from three facts, and the precedent RunnerSnapshot sets is to carry a fourth fact BESIDE the state - the last beat, the advertised labels - so a person can see WHY a runner reads as it does. Busy and parked reads draining; idle and parked reads parked; offline is decided first, because a parked machine that died is dead. The reason is a member because a runner taking nothing for a fortnight with no reason attached is the failure mode this most likely produces, and it is the sentence a withheld flight quotes back.

Three reason kinds and a fourth checklist satisfier, so a flight nobody can claim because the fleet was WITHHELD says which of the three ways it happened. Steps 3 to 6 of this slice each gave a person a way to make a runner take less work - reserved to its holder, directed at one machine, parked by hand - and each one made the surfaces that answer 'could anything take this flight' more wrong than they already were. A reserved or parked runner still counted as covering every label it advertises, so the apply-time refusal, the checklist satisfier and the waiting sentence all answered confidently and falsely. Shipping the first four steps without this one would ship a system that lies about its own fleet, and the lie is the worst kind: it reads as health while a flight waits forever. THREE KINDS RATHER THAN ONE, and it is the DeclaredAndAbsent / ForgeUnreachable split applied to the fleet instead of to a repository's narrowings. Somebody DECLARED a reservation and somebody DECLARED a parking; NOBODY declared a laptop being shut. Collapsing them sends an operator whose machine is simply closed off to go and check a configuration that is perfectly correct, and sends the person whose flight is queued behind a colleague's reservation off to provision capacity they already own. Different remedies, and a person who cannot tell them apart fixes the wrong thing - which is the whole argument ForgeUnreachable was added on. WITHHELD IS NOT A CAPABILITY GAP, and that is why the checklist grows a fourth satisfier rather than reusing one. 'nobody-declared-capability-gap' means the fleet cannot do this; withheld means the fleet CAN, is advertising exactly what is needed, and a declaration is holding it back. 'already-true-via-matching' would say the requirement is met while no flight can move. 'declined-by-bound' would say a strategy is managing it when no strategy is involved at all. Slice twelve's closure said the next value here arrives as a deliberate contract change; this is one. The item's whenUnmet reason says WHICH withholding, because withheld is the family and the reason is the member. EVERY ONE OF THEM IS `failed`, NEVER `refused`. Nothing was refused - the flight was admitted, it is in the air, and it is waiting for a person. Filing a withholding under refused would put a flight that is going to run in the same bucket as a document somebody was told no about, which is the rule NoRunnerAdvertises, PoolWarming, DeclaredAndAbsent and ForgeUnreachable are all already filed under. A RESERVATION NAMES A PERSON BY DISPLAY, OR SAYS IT CANNOT. TakeoverHeld.By settled the first half - 'somebody else has this' sends a person nowhere and a uuid sends them somewhere worse. The second half is a reservation whose holder has left the tenant: there is no expiry and nothing clears it but a person, so that runner takes no work indefinitely and the only thing that makes it visible is this sentence saying so. One parameter instead of two, the way a schedule clearing carries an eta or does not - a placeholder where a name goes reads as a rendering bug and teaches the reader nothing. A PARKING QUOTES THE REASON SOMEBODY GAVE, which is the promise 0.94.0 made when it made the reason a member: 'a runner taking nothing for a fortnight with no reason attached is the failure mode this most likely produces, and it is the sentence a withheld flight quotes back'. It also copes with no reason at all, because the member is nullable where it is written and a sentence that required one would fail on the parking made in a hurry - turning a governed wait into a failure of the surface meant to explain it.

A fifth destination kind - `flight` - whose act is that a flight EXISTS, and the member that bounds which work kinds it may open. FIRST CATEGORY, THIRD INSTANCE, and the safest of the four: envelope-change and airspace-registration are already performed by admission and land inside the tenant's own stream and registries; pull-request leaves on the customer's credential and check-run on the control plane's. Here nothing leaves and no credential is involved at all, which is what makes the whole design defensible rather than merely convenient. WHY THIS AND NOT AN AGENT NAMING ITS OWN KIND. The question was 'can an agent determine the work kind', and the honest answer was no - because a work kind is not a label on a flight, it is the selection of a governance regime. Loops, Destinations, Accepts and Produces are all work-kind-only: the sets are picked, not narrowed into being. So an agent choosing its own kind is an agent choosing its own moves, which is Article IX's failure wearing a convenience. A flight destination moves the decision to a place that already has machinery to govern it. The nominating flight runs under its OWN envelope - read-only, its own budget, its own destination - and what it nominates becomes a flight only by passing admission. `OPENS` IS THE WHOLE CONTROL, and it is why this is better than deciding the same thing in a client. It is the pre-approved menu, written by a person; admission refuses a nomination outside it. If it is ever defaulted to 'every declared kind' for convenience, the agent is choosing its own regime again with two extra flights and an audit trail that makes it look governed. It is refused rather than ignored on every other kind, which is the precedent sitting three lines away in the same validation loop: preserve-unadmitted is refused on anything but pull-request because 'a knob that silently does nothing on one kind of destination is a governance permission somebody sets and believes they granted'. Same sentence, different knob. ABSENT AND EMPTY ARE ONE ANSWER, deliberately unlike accepts:. A flight destination that may open nothing is a destination whose admission can never act - which is the unreachable destination ADR-0019 section 3 has asked to be refused at authoring since it was written, and which nothing had ever implemented. This is the first, and it is a small precedent as well as a control. Silence is a legal state for a document that is not a work kind; it is never a legal state for the key that IS a destination's only act. INTERSECT, ON MOVES' PRECEDENT, AND THE DIRECTION ARM IS WRITTEN BY HAND. A layer may only shrink what may be opened, because a name gained is a governance regime an agent can newly reach. The composer never consults the operator - destinations come wholesale from the base document and a narrowing cannot express one at all - so the declaration's job is to put the field inside the drift guard's sweep, and EnvelopeDirection's job is to read the direction. Both are needed: the guard that claims every composed field has a direction rule reads the operator table to check the operator table, so a field can carry an operator and still be invisible to the comparison. That is exactly what happened to accepts:, and for opens: it would have meant a classifier's menu of governance regimes growing with no approver anywhere near it. FORWARD-ONLY, AND IN WRITING. ADR-0019 section 1 is 'there are no sub-flights', and its prohibition is precise: a flight 'does not create another flight, hold a reference to one, or block on one completing.' That is a parent WAITING on a child. This is the opposite direction and must be kept there, because the next person reads 'a flight can open a flight' and builds a DAG: a flight destination opens a flight and holds no reference to it. Nothing waits on the opened flight, nothing reads its state, and grounding either does not touch the other. The two are related by sharing an intent and by nothing else - section 6's 'no rollup, no cascade' one noun over, with section 5's correlation-by-intent as the only linkage there is. WHAT THIS VERSION DOES NOT CARRY. Whether an opened name is declared in a tenant's topology, whether it plays the work-kind role, and whether it itself opens a flight are all questions about a tenant's OTHER documents. Envelope.Validate is pure over one document and is not even told that document's own name, so those refusals belong to the control plane's apply door - in both directions, because the offending pair can be authored a day apart. Declaring them here would have made the rule look enforced while half of it was not.

The wire surface half of the nomination: FlightNomination is a pinned type with declared JSON members, so it moves this fingerprint as well as the fact vocabulary's. The two version separately because they answer different questions - this one tells a consumer whether their client still compiles, and the fact vocabulary tells a runner whether the facts it can produce are the ones this control plane evaluates obligations against - and a change that adds a fact type moves both. See fact-vocabulary.json 0.18.0 for what the type is for and why it carries two members and no third.

loop.question - the question an agent could not answer from the work itself, as a pinned fact type with one member and its own slot on FactEnvelope. A MEMBER added to a pinned type and a new type registered, which is a version move rather than a breaking one: a reader built before it sees a slot it does not know and a kind it will refuse, which is the closure working. A FACT RATHER THAN A FIELD ON loop.outcome, because asking and finishing are two facts and not one state: an agent that asked and then went on to finish is `completed` WITH a question recorded beside it, and collapsing them would make one clarifying question turn a finished flight into a chore. ONE MEMBER, and the shape is a ratchet. Every field somebody will want - what the agent thinks it needs, which files, how long, where it should land - makes the question more useful and makes it configuration an agent writes. What crosses is a value, never a permission, which is the line LeaseFeedback holds travelling the other way. It decides nothing: whether a recorded question opens a gate is the envelope's to say through an ordinary obligation, because an agent that could open a gate by asking could stall a tenant's work at will.

TakeSeed.priorQuestion - what the previous attempt asked a person, carried to the next one. A MEMBER added to a pinned type, so a reader built before it sees a slot it does not know rather than a document it cannot parse. IT SITS BESIDE priorHuman BECAUSE IT IS THE OTHER KIND OF ASSERTION IN THAT DOCUMENT. One is a person's words and one is an agent's; everything else in a seed is measured. It is rendered marked as an agent's assertion for the same reason the person's account is marked as theirs - whoever reads a resumption is picking up work somebody else did, and an unlabelled block of prose among measurements reads as a measurement. WITHOUT IT THE ANSWER ARRIVES AND THE QUESTION DOES NOT. A rejected gate's reason reaches the next attempt through the feedback block; the question that reason answers reached nowhere, so a resuming agent was handed a reply to something it could not read - and would ask it again.

AttachmentConditions gains 'loop asked for a decision' - a fourth form, so an envelope can gate on a question an agent recorded. A VALUE IN A CLOSED VOCABULARY, which is why this is a version move: a reader built before it meets a condition it does not recognise and refuses the document, which is the closure working - a condition nothing recognises cannot be treated as false, because false is the answer that removes the obligation and records nothing. A CONDITION RATHER THAN A NEW PRIMITIVE, on the disposition 'envelope widens' established. What routes a flight to a person is a gate; the gate list is fed by gates and the queue a person reads is fed by the gate list. A surface beside all three would be a second way for a flight to need somebody and only one of them has a reader. It is also what keeps the question from deciding anything: the runner records that an agent asked, and whether that opens a gate is the envelope's to say. An agent able to open a gate by asking could stall a tenant's work at will. IT READS A RECORDED ACT, so it is monotone - a question that was asked stays asked, the same property 'moves used include' has and the reason both are safe to attach a gate to. A condition that could detach would take its gate with it, silently. A check: machine obligation may not carry it, refused at APPLY where the author is still holding the document: a machine predicate computes a verdict from facts and this condition is about whether a PERSON is needed, so the pair is a gate no evaluation can ever open. The same pairing 'envelope widens' refuses, one condition over.

AttachmentConditions gains 'loop changed nothing' - a fifth form, and the MEASURED tier beside the declared one. An agent that is stuck and does not say so still produces a run that touched nothing, and that is mechanically knowable without its cooperation: this is what a tenant reaches for when they do not want to depend on an agent choosing to ask. CHANGED NOTHING IS NOT HAD NOTHING TO CHANGE, which is the distinction the whole form turns on. A kind declaring it produces no change manifest cannot have changed anything, and a flight naming no repository has no tree to change - attaching to either would put every envelope-change flight and every read-only kind in front of a person. The distinction is carried by `produces:` and by the flight's own repositories, never by this condition guessing. AND AN ABSENT MANIFEST IS NOT AN EMPTY ONE. Empty is a measurement - the runner looked and nothing had changed. Absent is the absence of a measurement, and reading it as 'changed nothing' would attach this to every flight whose runner has not shipped yet. A check: machine obligation may not carry it, for the reason the two conditions before it refuse the same pairing: it says a person is needed and a machine predicate is what runs when one is not. That refusal is one arm for both now, and it names the condition the AUTHOR wrote rather than a fixed one - a shared arm naming the wrong condition would send somebody looking at a line they did not write.

LeaseClaimRequest gains an optional FlightId: one flight a runner asks for by name, or null for whatever the fleet has ready. A person flying by hand is a runner that wants a SPECIFIC flight - the one they just opened - and the ordinary claim has no way to express "that one", so a hand-flight without this is a race whose failure is not an error: the person waits at a prompt while their flight is cloned on somebody else's laptop. NO SECOND ENDPOINT AND NO SECOND VOCABULARY. The five claim states mean here exactly what they mean to the fleet - `pending` becomes "not yet", `waiting` still NAMES the repositories whose credential reference has not arrived, which is precisely the sentence somebody staring at a terminal needs, and `parked` still means a person withheld this machine. A sixth state added for the attended path would be the second lease path arriving under another name, and the closure of that list is asserted rather than described. It ASKS; it does not decide. Whether this runner may have this flight is settled on the other side, and there are SIX checks rather than the two that are easy to remember: an unresolved gate and a runner-less work kind live in a BEFORE INSERT trigger on the ready table, and a readiness floor, JSONB label containment, the flight's own directed runner, the runner's reservation and a live-lease exclusion live in the claim's own pick. A grant that writes no ready row fires neither, so all six are re-asserted where the grant happens - which is the whole of why this is not merely an optional field. And `flightId` writes as null on an ordinary claim rather than being omitted, because that is what every other optional member in this contract does and no JsonIgnore appears anywhere in it: what a reader depends on is that the three members it knows are unchanged and that an unknown one is ignorable.

Envelope gains Instructions - an ordered list of EnvelopeInstruction, each a block of text and the document that wrote it - and MergeOperators gains Append to compose it. THE ONLY TEXT REACHING AN AGENT THAT ANYBODY REVIEWED: a flight's intent, a rejection reason and a prior attempt's account all arrive unreviewed, while this arrives through a gated, versioned, direction-checked document. LeaseFeedback refuses to carry more than a sentence because 'a reason able to change any of those would be unreviewable configuration arriving one sentence at a time' - the envelope is where reviewable configuration is supposed to live, so text here is not that failure, it is the thing that failure was measured against. APPEND IS THE FIRST OPERATOR THAT IS NOT ORDER-FREE, and MergeOperators' own remarks had to be amended to say so: intersect, min and union are commutative and union would deduplicate two layers that happened to write the same sentence, dropping the one somebody wrote second on purpose. Appending in layer order is safe only because layer order is already total and meaningful - root, then work kind - which is a property of the composer's callers rather than of the operator, and a field composed across layers with no defined order could not use it. Ranked by role and then by name within a rank, so two callers composing the same layers still hash the same bytes. NEVER A WIDENING, declared explicitly rather than reached by default: EnvelopeDirection's static constructor throws for an operator with no ordering, and it fired when this field landed. Instructions are text an agent READS and reading moves no bound - they cannot enlarge a scope, grant a move, raise a budget or add a destination, because the manifest check decides those and rule 5 makes 'instructions cannot contradict the structured fields beside them' a disposition the prompt states. The cost, said plainly: standing guidance changes without the widening gate, which is the latitude a tenant already has over an intent and a rejection reason, and unlike those two this text is reviewed, versioned and attributed. BOUNDED IN TOTAL AND REFUSED AT APPLY: 4000 characters across all blocks rather than per block, because what an agent reads is the concatenation and fifty short blocks land the same wall of text. Refused rather than truncated - an agent reading half a policy cannot tell that it read half - and the refusal names both numbers so an author is not sent to count characters by hand. An empty or whitespace block is refused because a block that parses and says nothing is a policy somebody believes they wrote. PROVENANCE IS THE COMPOSER'S, never the author's, exactly as Obligation.Provenance is: guidance whose source a person cannot find is guidance nobody can change. NOT ON A NARROWING, and NarrowingSurfaceTests now holds EnvelopeNarrowing to its single member by name - the request that started this asked for instructions tied to a narrowing on work kind, and a narrowing declares what it ADDS with no member for what it changes, which is the failure a type without such a member cannot express. Optional rather than required, so no applied document is rewritten and an envelope declaring none renders unchanged.

LeaseLoop gains Instructions - the operator's standing instructions for this work, composed and rendered, or null. THE RENDERED TEXT AND NOT THE MODEL, which is the choice ResumesFrom makes one member up and for the reason written there: rendering at the consumer would be a second implementation of a document the contract already renders once, and two wordings for one policy is two policies. EnvelopeText.RenderInstructions is that one renderer - the control plane composes the envelope and calls it, the runner inserts the string verbatim, and a prompt test in the public repository is therefore asserting the wording that actually ships rather than a copy of it. ABSENT WHEN THE ENVELOPE DECLARES NONE, which is every envelope today: null rather than an empty string, because 'no standing instructions' and 'standing instructions that say nothing' must not read the same in a prompt - the same distinction ResumesFrom draws for a first attempt, and this project's most repeated defect. WHAT THE RENDERING SAYS IS THE CONTROL. Four kinds of text reach an agent - a flight's intent, a rejection reason, a prior attempt's account and this - and this is the only one anybody reviewed, so it names itself as the operator's STANDING instructions rather than advice from whoever opened the flight. An agent that cannot tell the reviewed text from the unreviewed gains nothing from the review having happened. It also states its own limits in the same block: an instruction does not enlarge a scope, grant a move, raise a budget or add a destination, and where one appears to, the envelope's fields hold. Rule 5 is a disposition rather than an enforcement - the manifest check decides - and an agent left to infer that would eventually infer otherwise. Each block is attributed to the document that wrote it, because guidance whose source a person cannot find is guidance nobody can change. PLACED AFTER THE WORK AND BEFORE ANY PRIOR ATTEMPT in the runner's prompt, which is a decision rather than an accident of concatenation: a policy read after a failure account reads as a reaction to it. An envelope declaring none renders the prompt byte for byte as it did before this field existed, asserted rather than assumed, which is what makes it safe to ship ahead of the walk that measures whether any of it moves behaviour. NOTHING POPULATES IT YET: the control plane half is not in this change, so no lease carries instructions and no agent reads one.

loop.attended - a twelfth fact kind, and the only one whose entire subject is what was NOT measured. A person held the terminal, so there was no stream to read: turns, moves used and the outcome are all required on ExecutorRun and all three would be invented. The executor answers null and this fact says what it could not see, which is rule 3 of the slice - no fact is emitted that an attended session did not measure, and absence is DECLARED rather than implied by a default. EVERY ONE OF THE THREE HAS A PLAUSIBLE, EXPRESSIBLE, SILENTLY WRONG VALUE, which is why the declaration is worth a kind. Attempts = 0 reads as it worked first time. MoveEnforcement = none reads as measured and unbound. MovesUsed = [] is the expensive one: `moves used include edit` against an empty list is FALSE, which DISCHARGES the obligation, so every move-gate on every hand-flown flight would report satisfied by never having been measured - nothing would throw and nothing would appear in a log, the gate would simply stop existing. THE GAP IS A VALUE IN A CLOSED VOCABULARY (AttendedGaps: turns, moves, move-bound) RATHER THAN THE KIND'S MERE EXISTENCE, for two reasons. Deriving "moves were not measured" from the presence of the fact is implying it from a default, which is the thing rule 3 names. And it would freeze the set: an executor that later measures moves for an attended session could not say so without a new kind, where now it omits one value. A reader meeting a gap it does not know halts, which is the only safe answer to "something else was not measured and I cannot tell you what" - an unrecognised gap carried on is worse than an undeclared one, because it reads as having been handled. A GAP NAMED WITHOUT A CONSEQUENCE IS A FOOTNOTE, so the budget and the time actually held travel on the same fact. Rule 6 records the envelope's wall clock for an attended session and does not enforce it - nobody's terminal is killed - so held MAY exceed the budget and that is a valid fact rather than a refused one. A validator refusing the overrun would leave only the flights that did not overrun able to report one. THE BINARY VERSION IS LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN DECORATION. The runner pins no CLI version - binary = "claude", whatever is on PATH - and the tool surface moved from 28 to 29 between the two versions slices twenty-six and twenty-seven measured. So `move-bound` is a claim about a NAMED BINARY AT A NAMED VERSION or it is a claim that expires quietly, on a machine nobody upgraded on purpose. THE RUNG IS THE LOOP'S OWN DECLARATION, CARRIED AND NEVER COERCED. An attended flight whose loop declares frontier records frontier: somebody sat at the terminal and an agent still did the work. Recording human because a person was present would make every later count of how much the machine did wrong in the flattering direction, on the one measurement this product exists to be honest about - ExecutorRungs.Human's own argument run in the direction that does not flatter it. IT NAMES NOBODY. Who flew it is derived from the session control-plane-side, on HumanAccount's argument and rule 8: a member here would be a runner asserting an identity, which is the one thing a runner may not do. And the shape is a ratchet on FlightNomination's argument - this is the one place a hand-flown flight explains itself, so every field somebody will want (the moves they actually used, the scope they worked in, an approver) makes it more useful and makes it an unmeasured claim wearing a measurement's clothes. Members are enumerated exactly rather than a forbidden list, because a forbidden list passes on the member nobody thought of. Settings sources cleared are NOT a closed vocabulary, deliberately: they are a vendor's names and they will move, nothing branches on them, so an unrecognised one costs a reader nothing - unlike a gap, where it costs everything. Nothing populates it yet: the runner half is not in this change.

LeaseGranted gains IntentText - the words somebody typed, when the flight is about those rather than about something addressable. WITHOUT THIS A TEXT FLIGHT IS LEASED AND NEVER WORKED, which is the sentence IntentProvider carries one intent kind over. A runner invokes on an intent that NAMES WORK, and typed words had nothing to offer: gg fly "<text>" cloned a tree, renewed twice and reported landed with no agent invoked and nothing said. Measured on a live tenant before this was written - every free-text flight it had ever flown recorded no loop.outcome, including three smoke tests whose own text says they verify the agent loop end to end. This is the third time the same silence has been closed: first Trees.Count == 0, then NamesWork reading only a uri, and text was named in both remarks and given nothing to offer either time. It is NOT the body IntentUri refuses to carry - that rule is about an issue's text, customer content the runner resolves with the customer's own credential, and these are the operator's own words which the control plane already holds and already prints in gg flights.

FlightNomination gains Note - what the nominating agent would tell whoever picks the work up, or null when it has nothing to add. THE THIRD MEMBER ON A TYPE WHOSE SHAPE IS A RATCHET, and the ratchet fired: the surface test enumerates members exactly rather than forbidding bad names, so this could not be added quietly. The answer to it is not that the field is useful, it is that it is a VALUE rather than a permission - the note grants nothing, scope and moves and budget still come from the envelope, and an instruction to exceed them fails at the manifest check. Advice, never authority, the rule Reason and LeaseFeedback already hold. THE BOUND IS MEASURED. Three real triage flights on a live host wrote notes of 728, 774 and 833 characters, the same magnitude as the reason's own measured ~700, so MaxNote is MaxReason and the test ties the constant to the data rather than to the constant beside it. Blank is refused and null is not: null says there is nothing to add, an empty string says somebody forgot, and a fenced block with nothing in it attributes silence to an agent. WHY CARRY ONE AT ALL, measured before it was designed: all three triage runs were given an item describing a defect that does not exist, all three read the code and found the described behaviour already correct, and all three spent the note saying which question to ask the reporter instead. A second agent starting from the item alone would have written the fix the item asked for.

LeaseGranted gains NominationNote - what the agent that nominated this flight left for whoever picks it up, or null when nobody nominated it. BESIDE Feedback BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME KIND OF THING: a person's rejection and a classifier's handover are both prose from outside this platform that a prompt must carry and must not obey. Advice, never authority - scope, moves and budget come from the envelope, and a note asking for more fails at the manifest check like anything else. THE HAZARD IS THE SAME AS Feedback'S AND WORSE. A rejection comes from a person the tenant employs; a note comes from an agent that read a work item, and in most organisations a work item is writable by more people than the envelope is. The path from item text to an agent's context is real and opened deliberately. What bounds it: the note grants nothing, it travels ONE HOP, it is fenced as an agent's words BELOW the operator's standing instructions in the same prompt, and a person sees it in the gate before the flight is opened at all. ORDER IS THE RANKING and the prompt states it rather than leaving it to be inferred. ONE HOP IS THE CONTROL PLANE'S TO ENFORCE and this member cannot: nothing on a lease can tell how many times a note has been forwarded, so the remark records it as the thing that side owes rather than letting a reader assume the type holds the line.

Destination gains MaySelect, a DestinationSelection of environments and repositories a nomination admitted here may name. THE ONLY NEW CONTROL IN THE SELECTION DESIGN, and it is a bound rather than a capability: naming an environment here grants a flight nothing, it says which of the tenant's already-charted environments a classifier may ASK for. Everything deciding whether the ask is legal already exists - the chart refuses an uncharted environment, ingress refuses an unregistered repository - and this is the door in front of both. What it stops is a classifier sending work to production when the tenant meant it to choose between two development environments. REFUSED, NOT CLAMPED: a nomination naming something outside these sets opens nothing, because clamping to the nearest permitted value would be the platform choosing where somebody else's work runs and reporting success. ON A FLIGHT DESTINATION OR NOWHERE, the rule Opens and PreserveUnadmitted already hold - a selection bound on any other kind is a permission somebody believes they granted, and the refusal names both kinds so an author is told what would be right rather than only that they are wrong. NULL AND EMPTY ARE DIFFERENT STATEMENTS. Null bounds no selection and asks an agent to choose nothing; empty says the tenant considered it and permits nothing, which renders no menu rather than an invitation to guess at names that will be refused. FIVE GUARDS FIRED AND EVERY ONE WAS ANSWERED: the composed-field table wanted an operator (intersect, on each leaf, the way opens does), the direction comparator wanted a hand-written arm for each set - an operator in the table is not a direction rule, which is the exact omission accepts: shipped with - the coverage sweep wanted real pairs that move them, the text-form ratchet wanted a YAML shape somebody can author, and the type vocabulary and wire surface wanted the new type declared.

LeaseGranted gains Menu - what a classifier on this flight may nominate, already rendered, or null when its envelope opens no flights. THE TOOL PROMISED THIS AND NOTHING PROVIDED IT. The nomination tool's description reads 'One of the work kinds you were offered', and the prompt offered none: an agent was asked to name a work kind it had never been shown, with a guess or a lucky convention as its only route to a valid name. Adding environments and repositories to that would have been two more fields to guess at, under a rule that refuses rather than clamps - so a wrong guess costs the flight. RENDERED FROM THE DESTINATION THAT BOUNDS ADMISSION, once, control-plane-side, and inserted verbatim: opens becomes the kinds on offer and may-select becomes the environments and repositories. A second list kept anywhere else goes stale the first time somebody edits the envelope, and its failure is an agent offered something admission will refuse. A SET THAT PERMITS NOTHING RENDERS NO HEADING, and an envelope that opens nothing renders no menu at all - most flights are not classify flights and their prompt is byte for byte what it was. Null and empty differ in the document and not in the prompt, because an agent told 'environments: none' would reasonably try to name one. IT SITS BELOW THE OPERATOR'S INSTRUCTIONS AND ABOVE A NOMINATING AGENT'S NOTE: a menu is a fact about the destination rather than guidance, so it does not outrank reviewed policy, and it precedes another agent's advice because what this flight MAY ask for bounds how that advice can be acted on.

FlightNomination gains Environment and Repository - where the work should run and which repository, or null when the classifier selected neither. DECLARED, NEVER PARSED: nothing reads a selection out of the reason or the note, because a governance decision made by a regex over prose that came from a work item is the path this design refuses. THE SURFACE RATCHET FORBADE THESE TWO BY NAME AND THE BAN IS LIFTED WITH AN ARGUMENT, written into the test rather than left in a commit. That list is about one thing: an agent may not ask for the REGIME its work runs under. Everything still on it is a piece of that regime - moves, scope, budget, obligations, approver, destinations, and `layer`, which would choose which envelope composes. An environment is not one: Envelope.Environment's own remark says 'a selection, not a bound', it composes root-only, it is validated for MEMBERSHIP against the tenant's chart and it is never merged. And the decisive part is what this type already permits - a nomination names a WORK KIND, which IS the regime, and that is safe because opens: is a menu a person wrote. Selecting where the work runs is strictly weaker than selecting what governs it, under the same kind of menu; refusing the weaker while permitting the stronger was the inconsistency. BOUNDED AT MaxWorkKind RATHER THAN MaxReason, because admission matches these exactly and anything long enough to be a sentence was never going to match a menu entry. Blank refused for the reason the note's blank is.

Envelope.Environment and .Repository become Environments and Repositories - sets of names flights may be about, checked by MEMBERSHIP rather than equality. A BREAKING CHANGE TO TWO MEMBERS, AND THE REASON IS THAT SINGLE-VALUED WAS UNIMPLEMENTABLE. The selection design has a destination permit a classifier to choose between dev and staging; it could not, because the bound held one name and FlightIngress required a flight's declared environment to EQUAL it - so a flight could only ever be in root's one environment. Every refusal in that design worked and the permission was unreachable. THE FLIGHT STILL NAMES ONE. A flight runs in one environment; what became a set is what the ENVELOPE permits, which is the shape Destination.Opens already has for work kinds: a menu a person wrote, an exact match against it, nothing outside it admitted. FlightNomination.Environment stays singular for the same reason. THE DIRECTION IS NOW ASYMMETRIC AND THAT IS A SEMANTIC CHANGE, not a correction. It was a SELECTION - what the flights are about - so a name where there was none had no declared order and any change was conservatively a widening. It is now a BOUND: writing one down where nothing bounded them RESTRICTS, so it narrows, and a gate for restricting something would make the cautious change the expensive one. Growing the set widens; withdrawing it entirely widens, because afterwards nothing is refused. COMPATIBILITY, DELIBERATELY. One permitted name renders as a scalar - `environments: dev` - so no tenant's document is rewritten on the next show, and the legacy singular keys still parse, because every envelope already applied uses them. Both spellings at once is refused rather than resolved: a precedence would mean the document says one thing and the engine reads another. An empty declared set is refused too - it would permit nothing while forbidding a flight from naming anything, a document that can only refuse its own work. AND THE LEGACY SPELLINGS ARE KEPT, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST. Applied envelopes are stored as this type's JSON, so every one already in a control plane carries "environment": "dev". A reader knowing only the plural would find no bound - and null here means UNBOUNDED - so an upgrade would have removed every tenant's environment restriction, silently, with no gate and nothing recorded. A widening applied by a deployment. Environment and Repository therefore remain as read-only compatibility members, folded in by the plural accessors so no caller has to remember, exempted from composition because composing one value under two names is how they come to disagree, and never rendered - so a document re-applied through the text form is normalised on the way past and the legacy member drains rather than persisting for ever. They can be removed once no stored document carries them, which is a question only a control plane can answer.

No surface change, and that is the point of the entry. A layer's silence now INHERITS a root-only bound instead of being read as moving it to nothing - one condition in EnvelopeComposition.Moved, no member added, renamed or retyped, so this row carries the same hash as the one above it. A BEHAVIOUR-ONLY FIX IS INVISIBLE TO A PIN, which is why it gets a version. good-grief consumes this package by version; without a bump the fix exists in the source at 0.112.0 and not in the artifact anybody can depend on, and the only way to get it would be to republish a version already published - two different packages under one number, which is worse than any duplication a version bump costs. Earlier behaviour-only fixes in this contract did not bump and were therefore unconsumable: the ten absorbing accessors and the Instructions NRE both shipped inside a later surface change that happened to carry them, which is luck rather than a practice. What this row buys is a number a consumer can name.

Declaring an environment or repository bound where none was declared is a WIDENING again. No surface change; this reverses a direction rule I changed on my own reading one version ago. When the bound became a set I read it as a restriction - bounding flights to dev where nothing bounded them looks like narrowing - and made null-to-anything not a widening. IT IS NEW REACH, which is what the airspace walk says in those words: the tenant's work can now run somewhere it could not, its flights compile a runner label they did not, and that is exactly what a reviewer should be shown. The reading had been deliberate since slice ten and an end-to-end test defends it; that test is what caught the change, after the unit suite passed with my rewritten assertion in it. WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW STAYS: direction WITHIN a set. A single selection had none, so any change was a widening; now growing a set widens, shrinking one narrows, withdrawing it entirely widens because afterwards nothing is refused. The rule is therefore: only removing a name from an existing set is a narrowing.

CurrentVersion, and GET /v1/version - the one door that may never refuse a caller for being too old. Every other endpoint declares ProtocolTooOld because the remedy lies elsewhere; this IS the remedy, so a 426 here would make the answer reachable only by the binaries that did not need it. The refusal and the cure cannot be the same door. It takes no session for a related reason - a host that cannot sign in may be the one furthest behind - and what the current gg is, is not a fact about any tenant, so the type has nowhere to put one.
