WHY THE CONTROL PLANE AND NOT THE FEED: `dotnet tool update` with no version takes whatever was pushed last, nuget.org repository-signs whatever it accepts (which proves the pipeline, not the publisher), and on Linux and macOS the client does not verify signatures by default at all - measured on SDK 10.0.102, not assumed. A host that asks the feed what is current is asking the party that would lie. This is the only independent channel. A VERSION RATHER THAN A DIGEST, for now: a version stops a fleet taking latest; a digest would also catch a package republished under a version that already shipped, which is stronger and needs the digest knowable at release time. That answer adds a member rather than changing this one. The single member is pinned in JsonMembers like every other wire type, because a rename there is a fleet that silently stops learning it is behind: the door still answers 200, the body still parses, the version reads as absent - which the client renders as 'not known' rather than 'up to date'. Correct, and permanently uninformative. LANDED AS 0.114.0 RATHER THAN 0.113.0: another branch published that number while this one was in flight, which is the collision CLAUDE.md names as happening here by construction. ALSO IN THIS VERSION: TenantNoticeCodes gains `binary`, so being behind reaches a tenant on the channel that already exists. A notice has one shape and three renderers - gg doctor turns it into a check, the console puts it on the queue row, the tenant page shows a banner - written once on the control plane so the three cannot drift into saying different things about the same fault; a fourth signal invented for this would be a fourth wording. Only the control plane can raise it: it knows what is current AND has received GG-Runner-Version on every request since the header existed, so it can already see a fleet drifting and has never been asked. NAMED FOR THE FACT, NOT THE CHANNEL - not `nuget`, not a forge - because how gg is distributed has changed once already and this code is meant to outlive the next change; what it means is that this binary is old. AND A NEW LIST, AdvisoryOnly, which is rule 6 fixed at the contract instead of promised: Blocking is otherwise the control plane's to decide and a reader may never promote a notice, but a control plane sending Blocking=true on this code would be contradicting the client rather than configuring it, and gg declines to be configured into breaking a build over a version number. The protocol floor's 426 stays the only thing in this design that refuses.

PendingGate gains a nomination: what an agent proposed, on the row the person answering the gate reads. The note it carries reaches the next agent's prompt, and a work item is writable by more people than an envelope is - so there is a path from an issue tracker into an agent's context, and a tenant putting a person in front of flight-opening with `requires:` is the only thing that closes it. That person could not see what would be carried. Approving was a signature on something unseen. ITS OWN TYPE RATHER THAN FIVE MEMBERS: flattened onto PendingGate they would sit beside the platform's own fields and read as the platform's, which is the one confusion a person answering a gate cannot afford - the renderer now has one thing to attribute and one null to check, and the heading says whose words these are. THE REASON IS REQUIRED AND THE REST IS NOT, and that is the discriminator: admission records why it opened a flight whenever it opens one and records nothing for a flight somebody asked for, so a proposal without a reason is not a proposal. Keying on the work kind instead would attribute a person's own choice to an agent, because flights nobody nominated carry one too. NULL RATHER THAN AN EMPTY PROPOSAL: most gates in an estate are on flights a person asked for, and a block reading "nominated by: none" over four empty fields would be noise on every one of them.

No surface change. This cuts a package carrying fact vocabulary 0.25.0, which adds the `transcript` gap to AttendedGaps - a vocabulary value is not on the wire surface, so nothing here moved and the recorded fingerprint is 0.116.0's unchanged. IT NEEDS A VERSION ANYWAY, and `unaided` is why the lesson is written here. That value landed in 0.24.0 of the vocabulary without a contract bump of its own, so no published package carried it until 0.112.0 was cut for unrelated reasons - and the consumer that wanted it pinned 0.111.0 by reading the source commit, got a package without it, and had to work out why from a CS0117. The pinned version is the source of truth and the release asset is what a consumer fetches; a change nobody can pin is a change nobody has.

A flight's story: FlightStory, StoryEntry and Actor, with GET /v1/flights/{ref}/story to carry them. ADDITIVE - /log keeps its type, its statuses and every kind it spells, because three walk scripts grep its JSON and a console fetches one per flight at boot. WHAT IT REPLACES IS THE UNION NOBODY ADMITTED TO. FlightLogEntry.Detail is documented as "a rendered string, not a nested object - a shape that varied per kind would make both of those parse a union", and what ships is a serialized dictionary with different keys for each of fourteen kinds. Every consumer parses that union anyway, and the line a person reads is `lease-granted {"generation":1}`. StoryEntry is Reason's shape instead: a closed kind, flat positional params, and one Sentence both repositories compile against - so there is nothing to branch on to parse and no surface can reword what another asserted. PROSE IS NOT A PARAMETER, which is why `said` is its own member. A halt's diagnosis, a takeover note and a runner's account of its own turn are sentences somebody wrote; interpolating one into a grammar is how a diagnosis becomes a guess. AND `actor` IS THE SECOND SPINE MADE A FIELD. A runner says what became of its own turn and the platform decides what that means for the flight, so no runner-actor entry may carry an ending kind - Validate refuses it. It also earns the story a fact the log structurally could not carry: the log omits FlightCreated unless admission opened it, because an entry for all of them would misattribute, and with an actor those are simply two entries. Three closed vocabularies join the contract fingerprint: StoryKinds, ActorKinds and FlightStages. Stage and state are different axes and both are derived - a halted flight stopped at `evaluated` and is `open`.

POST /v1/flights/{ref}/grounding and FlightGroundingRequest: a person stops a flight that could still have been done. ADDITIVE - nothing existing moves, and no client that does not call it can tell the difference. ADR-0017 declared this exit and left the verb, and WorkKindExits.PersonOperated says why in full: `gg ground is rare and every kind that motivated the slice finishes by admitting or by going moot, so the verb lands later - declared now, under no pressure, rather than invented in a hurry the day somebody needs it'. TWO DOORS RATHER THAN ONE WITH A FIELD, which is the ADR's carried-open question answered: withdrawing says the work no longer has a question to answer, grounding says the question is still real and somebody stopped the attempt, and an `ending' parameter would put the choice between two sentences in a caller's string where nothing type-checks it. The same statuses as withdrawal deliberately - what differs is which sentence is true, not how the door behaves. ONE CALLER, unlike withdrawal's two: pool recovery withdraws the maintenance flight whose pull point came back up, and nothing can ever ground one, because `a person stopped it' is a sentence no sweep can truthfully write.

RunnerSummary.RegisteredByPrincipalId: which principal registered a runner, so a consumer can tell its own runners from the fleet's. ADDITIVE and permanently OPTIONAL. The control plane has recorded a registrant since registration existed, but it is CurrentPrincipal.Display - text a person chose, which two people can share and either can rename - so grouping a fleet on it puts somebody else's runners in your group on a collision and drops your own on a rename. This is the id beside it, the same value WhoAmI.PrincipalId answers with, and named for it because that comparison is the only thing it is for. EMPTY IS A REAL ANSWER AND STAYS ONE: every runner registered before this shipped has no principal id in its stored event and no replay can invent one - fourteen of the fifteen on the development fleet - and a gg newer than the control plane it points at receives a payload without the member at all. Required would turn both of those into a dead fleet pane rather than an empty column, so it is init-only with an empty default.

RunnerSummary.RegisteredBy: the display name of the principal that registered a runner, beside the id 0.120.0 added. ADDITIVE and OPTIONAL. TWO MEMBERS FOR TWO READERS, and neither does the other's job: the id decides which rows are a person's own, because a display name two people can share would put somebody else's runner in your group and a rename would drop your own; the name is what reaches a screen, because nobody recognises a uuid. A consumer keying attribution on this member would be wrong the first time a name collided. TEXT SOMEBODY ELSE CHOSE - composed by whoever registered, travelling to a terminal - so a consumer strips control sequences before storing it, like every other display name on this protocol. Unlike the id this needs no repair for runners already in a store: it has been on RunnerRegistered since registration existed and the lens has always projected it.

RunnerSummary.ParkedAt and ParkedBecause: when a runner was withheld from claiming and why. ADDITIVE and OPTIONAL. BESIDE THE STATE RATHER THAN INSIDE IT, and that asymmetry is load-bearing rather than tidy: parking withholds CLAIMING and never touches a lease, so a runner can be parked and busy at once - which is the reason to park anything, letting a machine finish what it has and take nothing more. As a fourth value of State one of those two facts would have to be thrown away. The claim path made `parked` a first-class outcome because THERE the values are mutually exclusive - a claim was pending, or waiting, or refused because parked, never two - and that is why it is a state there and a fact here. WHAT THIS FIXES: the fleet read reported `idle` for a machine somebody deliberately withheld, collapsing exactly the two silences LeaseClaimStates.Parked calls the defect Waiting was added to fix. The control plane already stored parked_at, parked_by and reason and never sent them.

RunnerRetirementRequest and RunnerRetired: taking a runner out of the fleet. ADDITIVE. RunnerRegistry.RevokeAsync has existed control-plane-side since runners did - it sets revoked_at, publishes RunnerRevoked, and the fleet read already filters on the projection's Revoked - and NOTHING EVER CALLED IT. So the protocol could register a runner and never retire one, which is how the development fleet reached fifteen rows over two machines: twelve abandoned registrations of one pool host, left by repeated `gg runner up`. NOT MERELY UNTIDY: TokenLifetime is thirty days, so each abandoned row still held a bearer credential for the runner protocol surface. RETIREMENT IS NOT DELETION - the row stays and history keeps pointing at it, because leases name the runner that held them and the attestation ledger names the runner that attested; removing the row would orphan both to save a line on a screen. AND IT HAS NO UNDO VERB, unlike parking and reservation: a person changes their mind about withholding a machine, and nothing un-retires one - bringing it back is registering a runner, a different act with a different credential. The response carries WHEN rather than WHETHER, so `already retired` and `retired just now` are the same outcome and distinguishable facts.

The runner ask protocol: RunnerAskKinds, RunnerAsk, TailLogAsk, StatusAsk, RunnerSaid, LogTail, RunnerStatusReport and RunnerAskBounds. ADDITIVE, and DECLARED BEFORE ANYTHING CARRIES IT - ProtocolSurface.Endpoints names no route for any of it, which is ADR-0013's first constraint on Decision 3 rather than an omission: designing this around a transport would mean a second transport later cannot carry it, and adding the fallback becomes a rewrite instead of a registration. So there is no streaming shape anywhere - no IAsyncEnumerable, no callback, no continuation token - because the dead-drop is store-and-forward and has to move one answer, whole, once. THE VOCABULARY IS CLOSED THE WAY FACTS ARE, four ways: a pinned id, an entry in RunnerAskKinds, declared JSON members, and a slot on the envelope. That is what makes ADR-0013's read-only constraint a property of the build rather than a sentence in a document - widening the channel to a third kind moves this fingerprint and costs a version, which is the whole point, because the ADR's amendment expects the constraint to break and wants it to break deliberately. RunnerAskBounds is on the CONTRACT rather than in a transport so a second transport cannot disagree about how much comes back; a transport may be stricter and never more generous. And RunnerSaid.Stripped is here for ControlText's own reason - the control plane strips at ingress and gg strips what it renders, and those must be one rule rather than two that agree today. Line breaks survive a diagnosis and not a tail line, because a tail is already lines and a newline inside one would let a runner forge a row in whatever renders it. Contract ledger rather than fact ledger: these values are on the wire and never inside a fact.

The introduction: RunnerRegistrationRequest.PublicKey, RunnerIntroductionRequest, RunnerIntroduction, RunnerCapabilityClaims, RunnerCapabilityPurposes, RunnerSealedOffer and RunnerSealedAnswer. ADDITIVE, and PublicKey is optional so a runner registered before keys existed keeps taking work - it simply cannot be introduced, which reads as CANNOT rather than as no log. ADR-0013: the control plane says WHERE and WHETHER, never WHAT. It names the runner, says the caller may reach it, and says for how long; nothing that passes between the two ends afterwards is readable here. FOUR NARROWINGS AS FOUR MEMBERS rather than as a sentence - one principal (not a tenant, or anybody in it could answer as anybody), one runner id (not a label, which a fleet shares), one purpose and one expiry. The purpose is a CLOSED vocabulary with a single value: a free string would make "one purpose" a description of today, and the second would arrive as a typo nobody noticed. THE CAPABILITY BINDS AN EPHEMERAL KEY the console generated, so the runner can check that whoever it is answering is who it was introduced to - without the control plane reading either half. Ephemeral rather than long-lived because a standing console key would make every introduction linkable to every other. THE SEALED TYPES HAVE NO MEMBER A BODY COULD TRAVEL IN, which is EvidenceReference's own sentence about a different body: what is inside is the customer's private subnet addresses, host ports and egress IP, and this platform already declined to carry a hashed hostname as "an identifier nobody needs". Bytes rather than base64, because text invites a look. The answer carries no capability - the other direction is not a second grant. Identity is pinned at REGISTRATION rather than at introduction, which collapses trust to a single moment; the residual is that the FIRST introduction takes the runner's key from the control plane, and that is stated rather than left to read as stronger than it is.

Signalling rides the heartbeat: HeartbeatAccepted.Introductions, PendingIntroduction, RunnerSignalAnswer, POST /v1/runners/{id}/signal, and HeartbeatCadence. ADDITIVE, and `introductions` is ABSENT rather than an empty list so an idle fleet's heartbeat body is byte-for-byte what it always was. ADR-0013 wanted ICE candidates to trickle over the runner's existing poll rather than needing a push channel - and the poll was already here, along with the cadence control that makes it responsive: NextHeartbeatSeconds exists so a client respects a cadence rather than inventing one. A pending introduction shortens it. The runner gains NO new loop, no long poll and no listening socket, so its outbound-only posture survives by construction rather than by care - which is what makes ICE viable here at all, since neither peer may run a listening service. WHICH MAKES THAT MEMBER LOAD-BEARING FOR TWO THINGS, and HeartbeatCadence is what stops the second being usable against the first: a floor of one second so a control plane cannot make a fleet chatty at the runner's expense, and a ceiling of five minutes because an interval longer than the staleness bound makes a healthy runner read as offline - taking it out of the fleet with nothing having failed. The bound lives on the CONTRACT so the RUNNER can hold it: a bound only the sender enforces disappears the moment the sender is wrong, and the runner is the machine whose CPU and egress this spends. Clamped rather than refused, because a runner that stopped over an out-of-range cadence would turn arithmetic into an outage - and this repository has watched two loops die on a refusal already. PendingIntroduction carries the sealed offer and an id and nothing else; the id is NOT the capability, because the capability is what the runner checks and the id is what the answer is filed under, and one value for both would make a runner disclose its authorisation to say which question it was answering. The signal route answers 202 rather than 200: a route that waited for the far end would put the relay inside the conversation.

An introduction has two ends: RunnerIntroduction.IntroductionId, POST and GET on /v1/introductions/{introductionId}, and that prefix joining GovernedPrefixes. THIS CLOSES A GAP 0.126.0 SHIPPED WITH, and the gap is the useful part: that version declared the RUNNER's answer route and gave the console a capability and a key - with nowhere to put the offer it sealed, no way to collect the answer, and no id to file either under. An introduction is a short conversation with two ends, and declaring one of them is declaring half a handshake. It was found by the control plane's `every declared endpoint is actually served` guard rather than by review: following an unserved route led to the missing half rather than to a missing handler. UNDER /v1/introductions RATHER THAN UNDER THE RUNNER, because by this point the runner is not what is being addressed - one short-lived conversation is, and it outlives neither end of it. The GET answers 204 while there is no answer yet and 404 for one that never existed or has expired: a console polling has to tell WAITING from WRONG, and collapsing those two silences is this system's named worst failure. The POST answers 202 like the runner's half, because a route that waited for the far end would put the relay inside the conversation.

RunnerSealedOffer loses Capability, and RunnerSeal.OpenOffer answers with the console's ephemeral key beside the plaintext. THE REMOVAL IS THE INTERESTING PART. The member read as something the runner checked before decrypting - and the runner cannot check it: a bearer capability is verified by ASKING the control plane, and no route exists for that. An unverifiable field that LOOKS like a check is worse than no field, because it invites a later reader to believe something is checked. Found by building the runner's half of the handshake rather than by review. WHAT THE RUNNER ACTUALLY RELIES ON, now written on the type: the offer arrives on its OWN authenticated heartbeat, delivered by a control plane that already checked the console registered this runner and holds this introduction - and only this runner's private key opens the seal. The capability is the CONSOLE's proof that it may leave an offer, and it is checked where it is presented. So RunnerSealedOffer is now exactly the sealed bytes and nothing else, which is what EvidenceReference's 'no field a body could travel in' means applied to a frame as well as to a body. AND OPENOFFER RETURNS BOTH, because the runner cannot get the ephemeral key anywhere else: it is framed ahead of the ciphertext and nothing but the seal reads the frame, so a version returning only the plaintext would leave a runner holding something it could not reply to. Answering and knowing who to answer are one act.

RunnerSeal.EphemeralKeyOf: the public key a sealed message frames, read without any key at all. ADDITIVE, and it exists to CLOSE A HASH THAT WAS WRITTEN AND NEVER READ. An introduction is minted with the console's ephemeral public key and the control plane stores its hash against the row, under a comment saying the runner can then check that whoever it is answering is who the introduction was for. THE RUNNER CANNOT: 0.128.0 removed the capability from the offer precisely because a bearer value is verified by asking the control plane and no route exists for that, so the runner never receives anything to check against and nothing anywhere read the column. An unverifiable field that LOOKS checked is worse than no field, and this is the same finding one level up - left behind by the removal that found it. THE PARTY THAT CAN CHECK IS THE ONE HOLDING THE HASH, and this is what lets it: the sealer frames its public half ahead of the ciphertext, in the clear, because the receiver needs it to derive the shared secret. It is the address on the envelope and not the letter - no key is passed in, the nonce, tag and ciphertext are untouched, and a test asserts a private subnet address in the body is not obtainable from the frame. So the control plane learns which key sealed an offer, which it was TOLD at minting, and nothing else; the relay still cannot read what it relays. ONE READER OF THE FORMAT, not two: this and OpenOffer go through the same private frame check, because a control plane that accepted a frame the runner will later reject would file an offer nobody can answer - and a format duplicated across two repositories is a drift with a deploy between its halves.

FlightLaunchRequest.Attended, LeaseGranted.Attended and ReasonKinds.DirectedRunnerBusy: driving a runner is a flight. ADDITIVE, and both members are ABSENT rather than false so a headless fleet's bodies and leases are byte-for-byte what they always were. ADR-0013 decided that a remote hand-flight is three things and only ONE is new: a flight directed at that runner already exists - FlightLaunchRequest.Runner names a machine and the runner still PULLS - the channel is decision 3, and this is the marker that tells the runner to open one instead of running headless. WHAT IT BUYS IS THE WHOLE SECURITY ARGUMENT FOR FREE: the lease authorises, the envelope scopes, the story records, none of it invented for this. The risk of a debug channel was never that a runner can do dangerous things - it already runs an agent over customer code with credentials - it was capability without governance, a path no lease authorises and no story records. THE LEASE'S MEMBER IS DERIVED FROM THE FLIGHT'S AND NEVER SET BESIDE IT: two members that can be set independently are two that can disagree, and this disagreement is the worst kind - a flight a person is waiting at, running headless because the lease forgot to say, which reads as a runner that ignored them. THE RUNNER HOLDS THE LIFETIME rather than the control plane, because the machine that can end a channel is the one serving it; a control plane that merely declined to mint introductions would be a bound only the sender enforces, which is what HeartbeatCadence is on this contract to avoid. AND BUSY IS A REFUSAL WHERE ABSENT IS A WAIT, which is why they are two kinds in two families: an absent runner will come back, a busy one is somebody else's machine, and nothing in the pick checks for busy because a busy runner simply is not asking - so queueing would sit unbounded and then compete with everything else. A person at a terminal is the one caller who cannot wait an unknown time. Parking is not the alternative: the claim pump short-circuits on parking BEFORE the pick, so parking withholds every claim including the person's own attended flight.

StoryKinds.AttendedNobodyCame: an attended flight the machine never came for. ADDITIVE, and the vocabulary is CLOSED for the reason FlightStory.Sentence throws on a kind it does not know - a log kind the contract has not declared makes every story of that flight throw, which is a whole flight's history lost to a member somebody added on one side. good-grief's guard found this the moment the log kind existed there, which is the four-way registration doing exactly what it is for. AN INTERRUPTION RATHER THAN A STAGE, beside a takeover and a lapsed hold: those can land on a flight in any of the six stages, and this one can end a flight BEFORE IT REACHED A FIRST STAGE AT ALL - nothing ran. The sentence names the machine, because that is the only thing a person can act on: wait for it, or fly one that is free. WHY THERE IS SUCH A THING. An attended flight is one a person is waiting at a terminal for, and the launch check that refuses a busy runner reads the fleet and then creates a flight - nothing makes that atomic, so two attended flights can be aimed at one free machine and both accepted. This is what happens to the one the runner does not take, and without it that flight sits in the queue while somebody waits: the unbounded wait refusing was chosen to avoid, arriving anyway.

RunnerKeyOffer and POST /v1/runners/{id}/key: a runner offers the key it can be reached on, after the fact. ADDITIVE, and it closes a gap that made the whole introduction path unreachable on every machine that already existed. REGISTRATION IS READ-OR-REGISTER: a runner with a stored credential reuses it and never calls the registration route again, so the key RunnerIdentityKey.LoadOrCreate makes locally is never presented to anybody. Every runner registered before 0.125.0 was therefore permanently unintroducible, holding a key on its own disk that the control plane had never seen - and re-running `gg runner up` did not fix it, because there was nothing to fix it WITH. FOUND BY WALKING THE LIVE FLEET rather than by review: the key file was on disk, written minutes earlier, and POST /introduction answered 409 'registered before it could offer a key'. No test could have caught it - it needs a machine with a registration older than the feature. THE RUNNER PRESENTS IT, NOT A PERSON. It is the runner's key and it holds the private half, so it authenticates as itself; a route where a person supplied a runner's public key would be a route for supplying somebody ELSE's, which is the substitution the console's pin exists to catch. SET ONCE, AND A DIFFERENT KEY IS REFUSED WITH 409. Consoles pin the first key they see, so replacing one silently is exactly what a person watching for a changed key would never be told about - and a runner that lost its private half is brought back by a person registering it again, which mints an identity a console will notice, rather than healed quietly here.

OfferedConfiguration, OfferedSetting and the OfferableKeys vocabulary: a control plane may OFFER a machine configuration, and the machine decides whether to take it. A CLOSED VOCABULARY GROWS, so this is a version move rather than an addition - the only safe response to an unknown key is to halt. TWO KEYS AND THE ARGUMENT IS WHAT IS OUT, not what is in. stun-servers is a list of relay addresses and runner-labels is which work a machine advertises for; wrong relays degrade a connection and grant nothing, and labels can only ever offer to do less or different work, never more. Everything else is an instruction wearing configuration's clothes and is enumerated OUT rather than forbidden, because a forbidden list passes on the third member nobody thought of - FlightNomination's own reasoning. executor-binary is a control plane naming a program a machine executes, which is remote code execution. intent-readers' value IS a command line with a credential variable in it. vcs-hosts and destination-apis redirect where code is cloned from and where a proposal is opened. control-plane is a redirect and self-referential. pool-endpoint is the scope-enforcing proxy, and moving it removes the scope enforcement. A THIRD KEY WAS PROPOSED AND RETIRED BY MEASUREMENT: runner-hold-seconds is set by nobody on any machine counted, so it is surface with no need behind it. AND THE KEYS THAT DECIDE WHETHER ANY OF THIS IS ACCEPTED ARE NOT IN THE VOCABULARY AT ALL - that is the safety argument rather than a detail. accept-offered and accept-unattended live in the machine's own local file, are off by default, and have no environment variable either, so neither a control plane nor a container image nor a systemd unit can turn them on without somebody opening the file. A control plane that could offer them would be granting itself the permission. The offer is CARRIED on a response a machine already asks for rather than pushed: nothing connects inbound to a laptop, a runner heartbeats and a console refreshes. This version declares the shape and the refusal; nothing accepts an offer yet, and the control plane's half is good-grief's.

HeartbeatAccepted gains Offered: where an offered configuration TRAVELS, which is the poll that already exists. A MEMBER ADDITION, so a control plane one version behind is unaffected and a machine one version behind reads the response exactly as it did before - the member is nullable because absence means something, namely that nothing is offered. THE CARRIER IS THE ARGUMENT. Nothing connects inbound to a laptop and nothing is going to; a runner heartbeats and a console refreshes, so an offer rides a response the machine already asked for and the machine gains no loop, no long poll and no listening socket. That is the same reasoning the Introductions member one line up already carries for console introductions, and its remark states it: a runner's outbound-only posture survives by construction rather than by discipline. A ROUTE OF ITS OWN WAS THE ALTERNATIVE AND IS REFUSED - an endpoint for configuration is a second way to reach a machine and the start of the push channel this design exists to avoid, so AnOfferRidesThePollThatExistsTests asserts no such route exists rather than leaving it to a comment. 'Push' is what it feels like to an operator; a carried offer is what it is. Nothing here applies anything: the offerable set is two data-only keys and whether an offer is taken at all is a setting in the machine's own local file that this document cannot carry. The control plane's half - storing a tenant's offer and serving it here - is good-grief's, and this is the declaration that unblocks it.

OfferableKeys grows from two to five and SPLITS INTO TWO TIERS. A CLOSED VOCABULARY GROWS, so this is a version move rather than an addition. THE WALK CAUSED THIS AND THAT IS THE POINT OF HAVING RUN IT: 0.133.0 offered two data-only keys and refused five as instructions, and an operator asked which values they actually change across a fleet by hand named three of the five - vcs-hosts, destination-apis and control-plane. A need that real is not answered by keeping the refusal, and it is not answered by dropping it and pretending a redirect is data. So the set grows and the guarantee splits. OfferableKeys.Unwatched is the data tier - stun-servers and runner-labels - and only those may apply on a machine with nobody at it: wrong relays degrade a connection and grant nothing, and labels can only ever offer to do less or different work. The other three are DIRECTED, meaning they change where something is fetched from or sent to, and they may be OFFERED but never applied unattended - a person accepts each one and sees exactly what is being repointed, which is the control that makes offering them tolerable. Unwatched is stated rather than derived from All, so growing the offerable set again cannot quietly grow what applies while nobody is looking. WHOLE-OFFER, NOT PER-KEY: OfferedConfiguration.NeedsAPerson is true if ANY setting is directed, so one such key holds the whole document back including a half that would have been safe alone - applying part would make a machine's state depend on which portion of a document it agreed with and leave no single answer to whether the offer is in force. WHAT STAYS OUT ENTIRELY, because no person accepting makes it safe: executor-binary, because a path a person glances at is not review of what that program does; intent-readers, whose value IS a command line with a credential variable in it; and pool-endpoint, because moving the scope-enforcing proxy removes the enforcement rather than redirecting it. And accept-offered and accept-unattended remain outside the vocabulary, so a control plane still cannot grant itself the permission.

LoopMoves.propose-work-item, and GG-Fact-Vocabulary 0.26.0 with it. THE WIRE SURFACE DOES NOT MOVE - no type, no member - so this entry repeats 0.135.0's fingerprint, which is why the two ledgers exist separately: the contract version tells a consumer whether their client still compiles, and it still does, while the vocabulary version tells a runner whether the values it may name are the ones this control plane evaluates. It costs a package version anyway because the constant is IN the package: a control plane pinned to 0.135.0 cannot name the move, cannot classify it, and cannot admit what it produces. See fact-vocabulary.json 0.26.0 for what the move is and why it is record-only.

WorkItemOperations and WorkItemProposalLimits, and GG-Fact-Vocabulary 0.27.0 with the first. THE WIRE SURFACE DOES NOT MOVE - no type on it, no member - so this repeats 0.136.0's fingerprint, the same shape as that entry one step earlier: the contract version says whether a consumer still compiles and it does, and the vocabulary version says whether the values a runner may name are the ones the control plane evaluates, and those have moved. It costs a package version because both constants are IN the package and the control plane needs them to write a condition over an operation or to refuse a proposal for length. THE LIMITS ARE HERE RATHER THAN ON THE TOOL because the tool is not the only reader: the server refuses an oversized argument at the call where the agent can shorten it and try again, and the extractor refuses one in a transcript where nobody can. Two bounds would mean a proposal the tool took and the runner dropped. MaxReason is FlightNomination's, not a second guess: three measured triage runs put a real reason at 700-800 characters and nothing about a work item makes its reason a different size. See fact-vocabulary.json 0.27.0 for the menu and why it is not narrowed.

WorkItemProposal and FactEnvelope.Proposal, and GG-Fact-Vocabulary 0.28.0 with them. THE WIRE SURFACE MOVES THIS TIME, after two steps of entries that repeated their predecessor's fingerprint: a new type with five members and a new nullable payload slot on the envelope. ADDITIVE - a consumer built against 0.137.0 still compiles, and an envelope of any kind it already knows reads back identically, because the slot is one more nullable beside eleven others. What it CANNOT do is read a work-item.proposal, and that is the closure working rather than a break: an unknown fact kind is refused at ingress, loudly, which is the only safe answer. REGISTERED FOUR WAYS because three would cross the boundary as nothing - FactKinds, [PinnedId], Vocabulary.Types and ProtocolSurface.JsonMembers - plus the envelope slot and the FactCategories family, both of which the build refuses to go without. That registration is a bill this slice pays rather than work it invented; the guards are general and predate it. The detail member is a JsonElement, the first in this contract. It is what the fact vocabulary entry calls the field rather than the shape: opaque by declaration, bounded by size, and structured on the wire so the control plane stores something it can query rather than something it must parse twice. See fact-vocabulary.json 0.28.0 for why one member is opaque and only one, and why the score is not a number.

DestinationKinds.work-item-tracker and SubjectKinds.tracker. TWO CLOSED VOCABULARIES GAIN A VALUE, both on the Contract fingerprint rather than the Fact one, so GG-Fact-Vocabulary does NOT move - the first entry in this slice where it does not (steps 1-4 are 0.136.0 through 0.139.0 after rebasing onto the configuration slice, which had taken 0.133.0 to 0.135.0), because nothing about a proposal's shape changed. THE DESTINATION IS THE SECOND WHOSE ACT LEAVES THIS SYSTEM ON THE CUSTOMER'S CREDENTIAL. envelope-change and airspace-registration are performed by admission itself inside the tenant's own stream; flight opens a flight and nothing leaves; check-run leaves on the control plane's credential. This is pull-request's shape - the runner performs it, after admission, on a credential the developer registered - and it is the first that writes to a system nobody here owns, on somebody else's schema, through an adapter that maps our verbs onto whatever that tracker calls them. WHAT IS ADMITTED IS EACH PROPOSAL, NOT THE BATCH, because a triage ships one fact per change; a destination that admitted the batch would make 'the re-field but not the link' unsayable, which is the answer triage most often deserves. THE SUBJECT KIND WAS NOT IN THE SLICE'S PROTOCOL TABLE AND THE BUILD FOUND IT. Envelope.Accepts has to range over something and a flight reading a backlog is about neither a repository nor an envelope - which is exactly the argument SubjectKinds.envelope was added under, a shipping work kind with no honest declaration available to it, where [] says it is about nothing and [repository] says it is about a tree it never checks out. HasTree classifies it false, so the path bound is `none`; SubjectKinds' own remark predicted this cost as 'one classification rather than an edit to a refusal', and that is what a fourth kind paid. The subject is deliberately NOT the destination: a flight can read one tracker and be admitted to write to another, or read one and write nowhere at all, and conflating them would make 'look at this backlog and tell me what you think' impossible to declare without also granting a write. The sixth destination kind was argued into EnvelopeChangeTests' count guard, which asks for one.

TrackerAdmission and LandingDecision.Tracker: which proposed changes to a tracker may be performed, and the field whose absence means none. ADDITIVE - a consumer on 0.139.0 still compiles and reads every landing decision it already understood, because the new member is one more nullable beside Push and Admission. GG-Fact-Vocabulary does not move: no fact changed. A SIBLING RATHER THAN A WIDENING, and that is the decision. DestinationAdmission requires Branch, BaseRef and Slug; a tracker has none of the three, so carrying one on that type would mean making those three optional - which weakens the REPOSITORY path silently, since their being required is what stops a runner pushing somewhere nobody named. Two permissions, two fields, each refused by its own absence, is the rule Push and Admission already state on that same type and this is the third field under it. EACH PROPOSAL, NOT THE BATCH. A triage ships one work-item.proposal fact per change precisely so a person can take the re-field and refuse the link; an admission that said only `yes` would hand the runner a decision nobody made. The admitted set is named by the IDEMPOTENCY KEY the facts already carry rather than by a new identifier, because minting a second identity for a thing that has one is how two identifiers drift - and the runner already knows these, having computed them when it shipped the batch. AN EMPTY LIST IS REFUSED, which is the subtle half of absent-means-no. A destination that admitted none of them is an ABSENT TrackerAdmission; an admission object naming nothing is a control plane that decided and then failed to say what, and a runner cannot tell that from `all of them` without guessing - and a guess here writes to somebody's backlog. Bounded at 256, because a backlog triage is a person's afternoon and not a migration. AND Destination.MayPerform, which is the other half of the same design: what a tracker destination may have performed, beside what an admission answers. THE SLICE NAMED THE WRONG MECHANISM AND THE CODE SAID SO - it planned to evaluate Destination.Opens against a proposal's members, and Opens is a menu of WORK KINDS that Envelope.Validate refuses outright on every kind but `flight`, with the reason written at the refusal: a list that bounds nothing is worse than no list, because somebody wrote it believing they had bounded something. MaySelect is refused the same way. So a tracker gets its own menu on the same terms, refused on any other kind, and refused when ABSENT OR EMPTY because a tracker destination that permits no operation is one whose admission can never act - ADR-0019 section 3's unreachable destination, caught at authoring rather than by a flight that proposed a dozen changes and was told nothing. THERE IS NO CONDITION LANGUAGE, and that settles the rest of that criterion by construction. It also asked that a condition over the proposal's opaque member be refused at composition; a menu of operations cannot mention that member at all, so such a rule is INEXPRESSIBLE rather than refused. The alternative - a predicate language over a fact's fields - would put the decision about what a later reader may ask into a document written today, which is the one thing the opaque member exists to avoid. It composes by intersect and EnvelopeDirection reads it BY HAND, like opens and both may-select menus. A guard caught the omission: an operator in the composition table is not a direction rule, and a set that grows with no arm in the comparator is a bound loosening with no approver in sight - which is exactly how `accepts:` once shipped able to be narrowed with no gate. An operation gained is a kind of change an admitted flight may newly make to somebody's tracker, on a credential a person registered for a narrower purpose.

GET /v1/configuration/offered, and /v1/configuration joins GovernedPrefixes. THE ROUTE EXISTS BECAUSE A TIER SHIPPED THAT NOTHING COULD EXERCISE. OfferableKeys splits five keys in two: stun-servers and runner-labels may apply on a machine with nobody at it, and the other three are DIRECTED - they change where code is fetched from or where a proposal is sent - so they may be offered and never applied unattended. A person accepts each one and sees exactly what is being repointed, and that control is the entire reason those three were safe to offer at all. Then: an offer arrives on a RUNNER's heartbeat, the person is at a CONSOLE, and Gg.Runner cannot reference Gg.Client. The code that takes an offer was not reachable from the machine that received one, and nothing a person could run had ever seen an offer. A READ A PERSON STARTS IS NOT A WAY TO REACH THEM, which is the distinction the heartbeat rule turns on and the one I nearly got wrong. gg's own ratchet refuses a configuration route saying 'a second way to reach a machine' - reach is INBOUND, nothing connects to a laptop, and a verb somebody types dials out like every other verb in the declaration. That ratchet was pointed at the console's client while making a claim about the runner's; it now scans RunnerProtocolClient, where a configuration route would be a runner reaching for settings rather than reading what rode the poll it was already making. The heartbeat carry (HeartbeatAccepted.Offered) is unchanged and is still the only thing a runner may have. DEVELOPER, NEVER RUNNER, and that is structural rather than a note about today's callers: a runner presenting its own credential is refused at this door. NO REQUEST BODY - a machine describing itself to be answered specifically is how a tenant-wide offer becomes a per-machine instruction. 204 IS OFFERING NOTHING and there is no 404: one offer per tenant, always askable, so 'nothing is offered' must not share an answer with 'this route is wrong'. THE PREFIX IS GOVERNED, so the declaration closes over it - an offer can repoint a fleet's forge and destination hosts, so a route under it that nobody declared would be an unaudited way to redirect machines. That is the /v1/credentials and /v1/invitations argument applied to redirection rather than to a credential, and it is why this endpoint change moves the ledger when the others do not: GovernedPrefixes is hashed by the closed vocabularies, so the surface genuinely moved. ADDITIVE. A consumer built against 0.140.0 compiles unchanged and every existing route answers identically; what it cannot do is serve this read, which the control plane's own conformance tests will now say out loud. RENUMBERED FROM 0.140.0 ON REBASE, and the surface with it: main took 0.140.0 for TrackerAdmission while this branch was in flight, which this repository's own CLAUDE.md predicts happens by construction. The fingerprint here therefore covers both changes - it is this entry's own move plus its predecessor's, which is what a renumbered entry always means.

WorkItemFieldEdit and WorkItemProposal.Fields, with GG-Fact-Vocabulary 0.29.0. ADDITIVE: a consumer on 0.141.0 compiles and reads every proposal it already understood, because a MEMBER is additive where a closed vocabulary's value is not. What it cannot do is see which fields a proposal would set - and the proposals it would therefore drop are ones it could not have performed anyway, since nothing before this version had a menu to admit them against. WHY A CONTRACT CHANGE AND NOT AN ADAPTER ONE, which is the whole of this step: admission admits on NAMED members. The fields are what a destination's menu bounds, so the control plane has to be able to read them; in the opaque detail the check would fall to the runner, and the runner is not an authority. Slice thirty-six exists because slice thirty-five's `field` reached three system fields and no custom one, and this is the member that makes Custom.RiceScore expressible. See fact-vocabulary.json 0.29.0 for why it is a list of a named pair rather than a dictionary, and why a blank value is refused.

Destination.MayWrite and WorkItemFields: which field paths a tracker destination permits, and the ONE MATCHER that answers it. GG-Fact-Vocabulary does not move; no fact changed. IT IS OWED EXACTLY WHEN FIELDS MAY BE SET, both ways. A destination whose may-perform permits `field` and which names no path can never act - the unreachable-destination shape Opens already refuses. One that names paths and does not permit `field` has a list that bounds nothing, which is the knob somebody believes they turned: the PreserveUnadmitted precedent. And it is refused outright on any other destination kind, like opens, may-select and may-perform before it. A TRAILING-`*` PREFIX IS ALLOWED AND A BARE `*` IS NOT. A rubric that is deliberately open-ended scores a seventh field tomorrow, and enumerating them is a document edit per field. `System.*` IS permitted, which looks like the unsafe choice and is the consistent one: the safety in a menu is that a PERSON wrote it into a document whose widening a comparator shows them, not that this contract ranks namespaces by how frightening they are - Opens does not blocklist a work kind, and a forbidden list passes on the third member nobody thought of. A bare star is different in kind, because a menu permitting everything is not a menu. AND THE WILDCARD IS WHY WorkItemFields EXISTS. It turns three SET operations into MATCHING ones: composition intersects two menus, EnvelopeDirection asks whether one reaches further, and admission asks whether an edit is permitted. Set difference answers correctly in one direction and backwards in the other - {Custom.Score} except {Custom.*} is {Custom.Score}, a widening reported on a NARROWING. A governance rule that cries wolf is one people learn to approve past, which is worse than not having it. So one function, read by three, because three spellings of `does this path match this menu` is how a field becomes writable and unadmittable at once. Matches is a PREFIX and not a substring: Custom.* must not reach NotCustom.Thing.

LoopOutcome gains four token counts. GG-Fact-Vocabulary moves to 0.30.0 with it, because the type that grew is a fact; nothing else on the wire changed. See that ledger's entry for why the members are nullable and why there is no total - both are the same argument, that a number nobody measured must not arrive looking like a number somebody did.

The allowance surface: AllowanceReading, AllowanceWindow, AllowanceSummary, AllowanceList, the AllowanceWindows vocabulary, POST /v1/allowances/readings and GET /v1/allowances, and /v1/allowances in GovernedPrefixes. GG-Fact-Vocabulary does not move; no fact changed, and that is the point. ITS OWN RECORD AND ITS OWN PREFIX, which is PoolAttestation's argument unchanged: the fact plumbing is lease-welded at four points - the batch carries a generation, the endpoint is lease-scoped, the ship call takes a lease id, and the idempotency key needs a flight id - and a reading of what a machine has spent has no flight. AND NOT A MEMBER ON THE HEARTBEAT, which is the shortcut worth naming because the poll is already there and two other features ride it. RunnerHeartbeat is declared liveness only, deliberately, on the argument that a runner able to report something about itself can report it while dead. That hazard has a cost here rather than an inconvenience: a stale reading still saying `plenty left` would spend somebody's own allowance for them. So MeasuredAt crosses with the numbers and the control plane can see how old they are instead of believing them. A NAME, NEVER AN ACCOUNT. `allowance` is the string a person put in their own configuration file - not an account id, an email, an organisation uuid or a token. Two machines signed in to one subscription say the same name and their spending adds up; nothing checks the claim and nothing could, because a control plane able to tell two subscriptions apart would be holding something about them. TOKENS AND A CEILING, NEVER A PERCENTAGE. A fraction computed on the machine arrives as a number nobody can check; both halves crossing means a reader sees that a ceiling was configured, what it was, and what was counted against it - and the ceiling is absent rather than zero when nobody configured one, because nothing on a machine records a subscription's limits. THE WINDOW KINDS ARE A CLOSED VOCABULARY and the consequence is why: a reader that met an unknown window and carried on would simply not count what it held, and under-counting is the direction that costs a person their allowance rather than merely misreporting it.

AllowanceWindow carries four counts and derives its total, correcting 0.145.0 one commit later and before anything shipped. THE CORRECTION WAS MEASURED, NOT REASONED. `gg allowance` ran against a real machine's transcripts and reported 757,457% of a week's ceiling. Over 37,209 assistant messages in seven days the composition was: cache_read 17,660,352,647 (99.0%), cache_creation 144,720,335 (0.8%), output 30,999,990 (0.2%), input 74,396 (0.0%). 0.145.0's Tokens was the unweighted sum of all four, argued for on the grounds that any weighting would be `a guess wearing a decimal point`. That argument was right about weighting and wrong about its conclusion: an unweighted sum IS a weighting - 1.0 - applied to the component that swamps every other, and it is the one weighting the data rules out. What it measures is how much cached context got re-read, which is the cheapest thing a provider bills. SO THE TOTAL IS NOW INPUT + OUTPUT + CACHE WRITES, a stated approximation rather than a claim: the provider's real weighting is not published, and what is public is that a cache read is the cheap component and a cache write the expensive one. ALL FOUR COUNTS CROSS, and the EXCLUDED one crossing is the load-bearing part - a weighting nobody can see is one nobody can correct, so a reader who learns the real one recomputes without a new contract. AND A SINGLE TOTAL STILL EXISTS, which is AttemptLedger's rule: one derivation, however many readers. A window carrying only components would let a console and a scheduler each compute the number and disagree about who has headroom, and that disagreement would decide who gets work. Tokens is a derived property rather than an init member, so the two sides cannot drift.

Everything the floor, the override and targeting need, in one bump rather than three - each one costs a release and a re-pin in the control plane, and the three are one feature. AllowanceFloor, AllowanceOverride, AllowanceOverrideRequest, the AllowanceTargeting vocabulary, Envelope.Targeting, LeaseClaimStates.AllowanceSpent, WhoAmI.IsAdmin, and owners/floor/override on AllowanceSummary. GG-Fact-Vocabulary does not move; no fact changed. A FLOOR IS A FRACTION, NOT A TOKEN COUNT. The ceiling lives on the machines that report, and a person setting one means `keep a third of it for me` - which survives a change of plan where a token count does not. Either window may be absent: keeping a third of the week and nothing of the session is coherent, because a session refills in hours and a week does not. AND A FLOOR WITH NO CEILING IS UNENFORCEABLE, which is answered by stopping rather than guessing - fleet work halts on that allowance, loudly, because a floor that silently does not protect is the one outcome a hard stop exists to prevent and the fix is one line of configuration. THE CLAIM STATE IS THE THIRD TIME THIS ARGUMENT HAS BEEN MADE. A runner narrowed away inside the matcher answers `pending`, which is what an idle fleet answers; `waiting` split that once and `parked` again. `allowance-spent` is not `parked`: parking is a person withholding a MACHINE, and this is a subscription with nothing left - the same machine works again when its window rolls over with nobody touching it, and a person reading `parked` would go looking for who parked it. Every prior reader halts on the new value, which is the cost and is correct. TARGETING IS WORK-KIND-ONLY, because a work kind selects a governance regime; root-only would make one answer serve a triage and an implementation alike, and narrowing has no meaning on a choice of two. Absent means `any`, which is what every envelope written before the member existed already meant - and `any` is the honest name for `random`, because dispatch is a pull and the machine that gets the work is whichever transaction wins a SKIP LOCKED race. GIVING UP `least-spent` IS A WIDENING in EnvelopeDirection, including by DELETING the line, because a floor protects a subscription and least-spent is what spreads work away from one that is nearly spent. DirectionCoverageTests caught the absence: a composed field the comparator cannot read ships able to be widened with no gate, which is how `accepts:` shipped narrowable. AN OVERRIDE EXPIRES AND NAMES A REASON, both refused when absent: one with no end is a floor somebody deleted without saying so, and a blank reason is worse than none because the person it was taken from reads that sentence and a blank looks like an answer. Bounded at a day. `isAdmin` ABSENT MEANS NO - the one case where the language's default is also the correct one - and it is a hint for a client, never a permission: what a person may see is decided per request, and this only says whether to offer a surface that would otherwise be refused. It is the first privilege distinction in this protocol, which until now split machine from person rather than one person from another.

POST and DELETE /v1/principals/{principalId}/admin, and /v1/principals in GovernedPrefixes. GG-Fact-Vocabulary does not move; no fact changed. WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL: 0.147.0 shipped WhoAmI.IsAdmin, the gated pane and the override route, and nothing anywhere could set the bit - a feature with no front door, which is the assembled-and-discarded shape. THE FIRST GRANT IN A TENANT IS OPEN AND EVERY GRANT AFTER IT IS NOT. There is no seeding and no other way to set the bit, so a tenant with no administrator could otherwise never reach the surface the bit gates. That is a weak rule on purpose and it is SELF-LIMITING: the hole is open exactly once per tenant and closes the moment it is used. An endpoint that let any developer promote themselves forever would make the privilege distinction decorative, and a gate anybody can open is worse than no gate because it reads as one. MemberCredentialRedemption is the precedent - anonymous by necessity, single-use, spent on redemption. DEVELOPER AUDIENCE, and the runner audience would be a real mistake rather than a stylistic one: a runner's principal is the developer who registered it, so a machine able to grant would hand every machine its owner's authority to widen. NO BODY - the principal is in the path and the grantor is on the credential, so a body would be a second place to name who is being promoted, and the two could disagree. 409 ON REVOKING THE LAST ONE: a tenant that removed its own would be locked out of the surface the bit exists for, and the only way back would be the bootstrap, which is to say a stranger. 404 rather than 403 for a principal the tenant does not have, per the heartbeat route: a name that does not exist is not a fact worth confirming.

AllowanceWindow.Reported, ResetsAt and ReportedAt - what the provider's own meter says a window has spent, when that window resets, and when the meter was last asked. Three members, no value added anywhere, so every prior reader keeps working and an older machine simply reports neither. GG-Fact-Vocabulary does not move; no fact changed. WHY A SECOND SHARE, WHEN Limit ALREADY GIVES ONE. Nothing on a machine can discover a plan's token ceiling, so Limit is a number somebody typed and the pane said `no ceiling' until they did. The tempting fix - measure the tokens, read a percentage out of the executor's cache, divide - is WRONG, and the file it would read proves it: the meter keeps FIXED windows that end at a reset instant (five_hour resets at a time of day, seven_day on a calendar anchor) while the ledger sums ROLLING ones. Dividing measured-rolling by reported-fixed puts two different spans over each other and yields a ceiling that looks plausible. So nothing is divided: the meter's utilisation crosses as it was read. IT IS NOT A FRACTION OF Limit AND MUST NOT BE COLLAPSED INTO ONE. Both may be present and they will disagree, because they measure different spans and one of them is a guess at a number the provider knows. Two members is what lets a screen say which kind of number it is showing; one member would make `40%' unattributable. ResetsAt IS LOAD-BEARING, not decoration: a share and a token count on one line read as one measurement, and the reset instant is the only thing that says they are two. ABSENT MEANS THE METER SAID NOTHING - every machine not running an executor that keeps one - and never nought percent, which is Limit's own rule and the one the 757,457% correction was written under: a zero reads as a plan nobody has touched. AND ReportedAt, WHICH THE ROLLOVER RULE CANNOT REPLACE. ResetsAt catches the unambiguous staleness - a window that has already ended, whose share says nothing about the one a person is in - and that case is real: measured on this machine the meter was fetched at 20:55Z, its five-hour window reset at 00:10Z, and at 04:08Z the pane printed `9% spent' about a window four hours gone. But a WEEKLY number can be hours old against a reset three days out, which no rollover rule sees, so the age crosses too and the pane states it. Report rather than decide: no threshold is invented anywhere, and a person is told how old the number is instead of being shown a number that has quietly stopped being true.

THE WIRE SURFACE DID NOT MOVE, and this row exists to say so. AllowanceShares - how spent a window is, by the provider's share where it is about the window in force and by a typed ceiling where it is not. No member, no endpoint and no value changed; the fingerprint below is 0.149.0's, unchanged. WHY A VERSION AT ALL, THEN: this package is how the two repositories share anything. gg renders this on four surfaces and the control plane decides two things with it - whether a floor has been reached, and which machine is least spent - and they cannot reference each other, so a rule written anywhere else is written twice. Four copies inside gg alone had already drifted once, and across repositories the drift shows up as a pane and a refusal describing different plans. A consumer seeing this number move learns that behaviour they share has changed even though nothing they serialize has, which is a thing worth being able to learn. THE PREFERENCE IS THE RULE: the provider's share first, because a typed ceiling is a guess at a number the provider knows and nothing on a machine can discover the real one. A ROLLED-OVER SHARE LOSES TO THE GUESS, which is the case with teeth - the meter keeps fixed windows, so a share from one that has ended would halt a plan that just refilled or lend from one that is exhausted, while the typed ceiling is at least about now. And neither answering means null rather than nought, because nought reads as a plan nobody has touched and a caller that cannot act on absence has to say so itself.

POST /v1/allowances/readings/mine - the same AllowanceReading, attested by the person whose subscription it is rather than by a machine. Developer audience, 202, session header. THE WIRE SURFACE DOES NOT MOVE and the fingerprint below is 0.150.0's: this is a new endpoint under an EXISTING governed prefix, and GovernedPrefixes is hashed into that surface while endpoints are not. The version moves because the control plane cannot serve a route it cannot see declared. WHY THE MACHINE-ONLY ROUTE WAS WRONG. Nothing ever argued for it. The declaration beside it argues three adjacent choices at length - why a reading is not a fact, why it does not ride the heartbeat, why 202 - and the audience is justified nowhere; it was inherited from the opening words of its own comment, `WHAT THIS MACHINE HAS SPENT', which presuppose a machine rather than argue for one. AND IT DEFENDED NOTHING: registering a runner is a developer act, so anybody with a session could already mint a credential and post whatever reading they liked, and the attribution is identical either way because the owner of a runner's reading is the developer who registered it. Nor is a machine's reading more trustworthy - this side has no transcripts, no meter and no ceiling of its own, and believes what it is told either way. WHAT IT COST IS REAL: an allowance is a person's SUBSCRIPTION and the meter measures the plan, so a laptop reading its own meter knows something true whether or not it ever takes a flight. A SECOND PATH RATHER THAN A SECOND AUDIENCE, because Audience is a closed vocabulary and a combined value would halt every reader that has one - and a machine reporting itself really is a different act from a person reporting what they speak for. THE MACHINE'S ROUTE IS UNCHANGED: widening who may report does not widen what a machine may do, which is the whole point of the runner audience.

TWO REASON KINDS FOR A CREDENTIAL A FLIGHT CANNOT GET. The diagnosis was already precise and nothing could render it: CredentialResolutionFailure carries the reference - kind, locator, identity, scopes - and a sentence, and the control plane records it on the flight log as `credential-unresolved`. But there was no reason kind for it, and Reason.Sentence THROWS on a kind it does not know, so the `why` line every other halt renders could never say "this needs a credential" at all. gg doctor names the gap in its own words: it fails at the runner where nobody is looking. TWO RATHER THAN ONE, which is the split declared-and-absent and forge-unreachable already make. `no-credential-registered` is a tenant who has not registered a reference - what ClaimResult.Waiting and LeaseGranted.UnresolvedRepos already carry - and names the repositories rather than counting them, for WaitingOn's own reason. `credential-unreadable` is a reference that IS registered and a machine that cannot read the secret, and it names the machine, because the machine is the remedy: `gg credential add` run a second time on the laptop that already holds it changes nothing and would look like it should. BOTH ARE `failed`, NEVER `refused`. A halt is not a refusal - the flight was admitted and the world cannot satisfy it yet - which is the rule every other waiting kind is already filed under.

THE THIRD RUNNER ASK KIND, AND IT IS THE ONE ADR-0013 PRICED. RunnerAskKinds said so out loud: "Read-only, for now, and the 'for now' is recorded rather than implied. ADR-0013's amendment decides that driving a runner is a flight, so this vocabulary is expected to grow - and when it does it will be through a lease and an envelope, not by a third value appearing here quietly." `configure-credential` is that value, and this row is what it cost. WHY THERE IS NO OTHER WAY IN: three doors are shut on purpose and each is recorded. A strategy document cannot hold a credential (StrategyContainmentTests, by shape rather than by string); an offered configuration cannot carry one (OfferableKeys excludes the intent readers because their value IS a command line with a credential variable in it); and a pool member has no file an operator can reach, which is why accept-unattended was retired as a switch for a machine that could not reach it. What was left was rebuilding the image for every rotation. ConfigureCredentialAsk IS THE ONE TYPE ON THIS CONTRACT THAT CARRIES A SECRET, and Article VIII is not bent by it: the control plane stores references and facts and never sees this, which crosses a channel sealed end to end between a console and a runner through a relay that says where and whether, never what. The safety is structural rather than intended - no endpoint in ProtocolSurface.Endpoints names the type transitively, so there is no request body it can enter, and the channel's serializer context is kept apart from the one a runner speaks to its control plane with. What comes back is ConfiguredCredential: a locator and a bool, with no member a value could be echoed in. IT IS NOT `RunCommand`, which ADR-0013 names and RunnerAskClosureTests plants by name: this performs nothing, returns no data, and writes one file the runner already writes for itself - it widens what a runner may be TOLD, not what it may be made to DO. RunnerCapabilityPurposes gains its second value, `configure-this-runner`, because an introduction minted to read a log must not also place a credential. IT IS NOT A CHECK THE RUNNER PERFORMS, and that is written down where a later reader will look: RunnerSealedOffer already records why the capability was taken out of the offer - a bearer capability is verified by ASKING the control plane and there is no route for that, and an unverifiable field that looks like a check is worse than no field. What restrains the runner is the closed dispatch and the lease.

A TENANT CAN TELL ITS RUNNERS TO FORGET A CREDENTIAL, which is the other half of placing one and the half that has to work with nobody present. Putting a credential on a machine is a person's act over an introduced channel, inside a flight; taking one back is revocation, and revocation that needs somebody at a terminal is revocation that happens on Monday. So HeartbeatAccepted.Forget rides the poll, where signalling already rides: a runner gains no new loop, no long poll and no listening socket, so its outbound-only posture survives by construction rather than by care. ARTICLE VIII IS UNTOUCHED AND THIS WAS ALWAYS THE SAFE DIRECTION. What travels is locators, which are references - the control plane already holds them and already sends them on a lease, so naming one to be DROPPED is strictly less than naming one to be used. It grants nothing a hostile control plane did not already have: the worst outcome is flights failing for want of a credential, and a control plane that wanted that could simply stop granting leases. That failure is legible now in a way it was not, because credential-unreadable names the locator and the machine. ACTED ON WHETHER OR NOT A FLIGHT IS IN THE AIR, unlike either neighbour on this type. An introduction needs a lease to authorise it and an offer is taken only while idle because acting on one ends the process. A revoked credential is revoked while the machine is busy, and a runner that waited for a gap in its work would hold a live secret for exactly as long as it was useful to somebody. NOT GATED BY accept-configured, and the asymmetry is the design: a machine has to agree to be GIVEN a secret, because that is somebody else putting something on it, and nobody has to agree to have one taken away - revocation a host can decline is revocation that did not happen. Two separate runner ports, so wiring one cannot wire the other by accident. Each locator is validated by the contract's own rule before it becomes a path, because deleting is the direction where steering one would cost the most, and one that will not drop does not stop the rest - a control plane repeats a revocation until it is sure, so an already-gone locator is the ordinary case. ABSENT WHEN EMPTY, the rule Introductions and Offered already follow, and the one where absence matters most: a runner ahead of its control plane reads a missing member on every beat, and a reader that took absence for "drop everything" would empty a fleet's credential stores the first time the two repositories were a version apart. NOTHING REPORTS WHAT IT DROPPED, which is AnAcceptedOfferIsRecordedTests' shape for the other direction: a machine that told its control plane what it accepted would turn a carried offer into a tracked instruction.

0.155.0 rather than 0.153.0: main took 0.153.0 AND 0.154.0 while this branch was in flight, which this repo conflicts over by construction - two contract changes in flight always meet here. RunnerStatusReport.FlightNumber and BeatAt - what a runner says about itself while somebody is watching it wait. BECAUSE A WATCH NOW OUTLIVES A FLIGHT. A channel to a runner used to exist only while one flight did, so what the tail carried could not change subject under a reader; a watcher attached to an idle machine follows whatever it claims next, and a pane that silently begins drawing a different flight's output is lying by omission. FlightNumber is what says it changed. THE NUMBER AND NOT THE ID: GG-84 is what a person reads and what RunnerSummary.CurrentFlightNumber already carries, while the id is only what the runner builds a live-view path out of - it needs that on the machine and nothing off the machine has a use for it, so sending both would put an identifier on the wire for no reader. NULL IS IDLE, NOT UNKNOWN, because requiring it would force a sentinel and every sentinel would then have to be told apart from a flight number by whoever read it. BeatAt IS A SECOND SILENCE: At says this channel answered, BeatAt says the machine is still talking to the control plane, and a runner reachable over a peer connection while partitioned from the control plane reads as healthy on the first and stopped on the second - only one of those is going to be given work, which is what a person decides on before they wait any longer. TWO MEMBERS, NO VALUE: RunnerAskKinds is unchanged at two verbs, so nothing that reads this surface has to halt - a member may be added freely where a value may not.

A CONSOLE CAN SAY WHAT AN INTRODUCTION IS FOR, and until now it could not. `configure-this-runner` shipped in 0.153.0 with the ask kind that needed it, and RunnerIntroductionRequest carried only an ephemeral key - so a console had no way to name a purpose and the control plane minted `tail-your-own-log` for every introduction ever made. A closed vocabulary with a member nothing can reach is the `port nothing calls` shape, on the half of the surface that is supposed to BE the narrowing. IT COST NOTHING, WHICH IS THE REASON TO FIX IT RATHER THAN SHRUG. The runner cannot verify a capability at all - RunnerSealedOffer records why one was taken out of the offer: an unverifiable field that looks like a check is worse than no field. So a purpose buys the control plane's refusal and the flight log's record of what a console said it was for, and neither could happen while the console could not say. What restrains a write on the machine is still the machine's own accept-configured. NULLABLE, because the two repositories are not upgraded in step. A console that predates this member sends none and must go on being introduced exactly as it was, so RunnerCapabilityPurposes.Requested resolves absence to `tail-your-own-log` rather than refusing it - anything else changes what an old console gets without that console changing. The resolve-and-refuse rule lives on the contract for RunnerSeal's reason: one rule both sides compile against, rather than two that agree today and drift. Refused turns away a value nobody declared and names what this build knows, which is the closure's own argument - a free string would make "one purpose" a description of today. AND THE PURPOSES ARE NAMED ON EACH CALLER rather than written at the call site: WatchARunner.Purpose is tail-your-own-log and SendACredential.Purpose is configure-this-runner. A literal in the middle of a method is a decision nothing can assert about, and the assertion that matters is that the two DIFFER - a test checking each against a constant would go green on the state this change exists to end.

A RUNNER SAYS ON ITS BEAT WHETHER IT WILL KEEP A CREDENTIAL, so nobody types a secret for a machine that will not take it. Until now the refusal arrived AFTER the value had been read, sealed and sent: the answer lives in the machine's own `accept-configured` and the control plane had never been told it, so a person found out by being told the runner heard and did not keep it - having already produced the token. IT IS NOT THE AUTHORISATION AND DOES NOT PRETEND TO BE. Only the principal who REGISTERED a runner may be introduced to it, and that is what answers "may this caller". This answers whether the machine will take one from anybody, which is a different question and the machine's own to answer. What it changes is WHEN a person finds out, not who may ask. A LIE GAINS NOTHING, which is why a runner may be trusted to say it: one that claims to accept and then refuses is exactly where this path already was, and one that claims not to accept is simply not offered the chance. The file on the machine still decides. AND THE CLAIM CANNOT DRIFT FROM THE BEHAVIOUR, because the runner derives it from the port the dispatch actually uses rather than reading the file a second time - a second reading is a second answer, and the failure that produces is the one this exists to end. THREE STATES, NOT TWO. Absent is a runner that predates this member, and a control plane that read absence as "no" would make every machine in the field unconfigurable the day it shipped; absence means mint and let the far end refuse, which is what happens today. The heartbeat's own rule is unchanged: it carries liveness and capability, never what the machine holds - a bool saying "I would keep one" is a fact about configuration, and a member naming WHICH credentials it holds would be a fact about the customer nobody agreed to publish.

A WORK KIND CAN SAY WHAT IT IS FOR, IN ONE LINE, AND UNTIL NOW NOTHING COULD. The names are a tenant's own words - score-hal, triage, implement - and a person being asked which of them a flight is for is being asked to pick between strings they may never have seen. Everything else an envelope carries governs an AGENT; this is the one member written for the person choosing. IN THE DOCUMENT, BECAUSE THAT IS WHERE THE KIND IS DEFINED. A description kept anywhere else drifts from the obligations and loops it describes; here it is changed by whoever changes them, in the same file and the same review, and it round-trips through pull and apply like every other key. WORK-KIND-ONLY IS THE WHOLE COMPOSITION RULE: root describes nothing in particular and a narrowing narrows something already described, so a description that composed would give every kind the floor's sentence or let a narrowing overwrite the kind's. IT GOVERNS NOTHING, and the comparator never reads it - no obligation, no loop bound, no prompt - so adding, rewording or removing it is never a widening in either direction. What that lets a tenant do, said out loud: reword what a kind says it is for without a human gate, which is the same latitude they already have over an instruction block. The alternative is an approval for a typo. TopologyName GAINS IT TOO, because that is where a picker reads it: a console listing a tenant's kinds holds the topology and nothing else, and fetching an envelope per row to find one sentence would be a read per name every time somebody opens the question. NULLABLE ON BOTH, because the two repositories are not upgraded in step and because every envelope that exists today has none - a key emitted empty would be a diff nobody made in every working copy on the next pull.

A FLIGHT SAYS WHICH KIND OF WORK IT IS, AND UNTIL NOW ONLY THE CONTROL PLANE KNEW. A launch has carried a work kind since work kinds existed - FlightLaunchRequest.WorkKind, defaulted to `implement` when a caller names none - and it decides which envelope governs the flight. The control plane stored it all along in its own read model and never put it on the wire, so every reader of a flight list drew a triage and an implement identically. THE NAME IS NOT THE KIND, which is why the name was not enough: `Name` is what somebody CALLED the flight and the kind is what governs it, and two flights called "fix the import" can be bound by entirely different obligations. A queue exists to tell work apart, and this is the field that does it. NULLABLE, because the two repositories are not upgraded in step and because a reader must be able to say it was not told. `implement` is what the control plane substitutes at CREATION, so a client filling an absent value in with it would be right by coincidence for new flights and a fabrication for every summary from a control plane that predates this member - on the one field that says which envelope governs. gg renders the absence as `(not said)` rather than guessing. NOT A CLOSED VOCABULARY. Work kinds are a tenant's own words - score-hal, triage - so this is the topology name as declared, and a closure here would describe today. It governs nothing on its own: it is a projection of the choice already recorded at launch, so nothing reads it to decide what a flight may do.

A WORK KIND CAN SAY WHAT A FLIGHT OF THAT KIND IS TO DO, AND UNTIL NOW THE RUNNER SAID IT FOR EVERYBODY. ClaudeCodeExecutor opened every prompt with "Make the code changes it asks for" whatever the kind, and the kind's instructions were appended after it as standing policy - so score-hal, which writes a number to a tracker field and changes no code at all, sent its agent to find the files a bug report named. The agent reported back that it had been "asked to make the code changes". It was. THE DOCUMENT COULD NOT SAY OTHERWISE, which is why score-hal's author tried to say it in the wrong place: half that kind's instructions are task statements wearing policy's clothes - "score that item and no other", "the score is written to Custom.HAL and to no other field" - and they lose, because the hardcoded imperative comes first and names the job. An envelope could say what a flight ACCEPTS, PRODUCES and may LAND, and never what it is to do.
