IT IS NOT Instructions, and the difference is which question each answers: instructions are standing policy about how ANY job is done, carried verbatim because they are the one reviewed text an agent sees; this is the job, and it REPLACES the sentence rather than joining it. Two imperatives and an agent picks one, and the one that reads as the job is whichever came first. IT IS NOT Description either, whose own remark says it governs nothing and an agent is never shown it, "so a wrong one misleads a person and cannot misgovern a flight" - driving the whole job from it would take away the property it was given to have. WORK-KIND-ONLY: root is not any one job and a narrowing narrows a job already named, so a brief that composed would hand every kind the floor's task or let a narrowing rewrite the kind's. NEVER A WIDENING IN EITHER DIRECTION, for Instructions' reason: nothing an agent READS decides what a flight may reach, and scope, moves, destinations and admission still refuse exactly what they refused before - a brief telling an agent to push is refused by the destination it does not have. NULLABLE ON BOTH Envelope AND LeaseLoop, because the two repositories are not upgraded in step and because every work kind in the field states none: absence renders the wording those flights have always been given, byte for byte, and a member that re-aimed them by arriving would be worse than the defect it fixes.

A FLIGHT MAY NAME MORE THAN ONE REPOSITORY, AND EVERY OTHER END COULD ALREADY CARRY THEM. FlightRepo has been a list on the wire since it was written, IWorkspace.PrepareAsync takes that list and answers with WorkspaceResult.Trees plural, every tree is cloned and observed, and the envelope's repository bound has been a SET since 0.112.0. The only end that could never say two was the flight itself - and the only tree an agent was ever told about was the first. WHAT THAT COSTS, MEASURED: a work kind whose procedure lives in one repository and whose subject lives in another - a scoring rubric at .claude/skills/hal/ in one, the item's code in the other, which that kind's own instruction says in as many words - could name only the one it was pinned to. Its agent read the item, confirmed it was in scope, and stopped: "I don't have the HAL rubric ... this flight is pinned to the JDNext working tree." BESIDE Repository RATHER THAN REPLACING IT. The singular is what every client that has ever opened a flight sends, and a control plane reading only the plural would drop the repository off every one of them; a client naming exactly one still fills the singular, so nothing that works today travels differently. ORDER IS CARRIED, NOT SORTED: they are cloned in it and listed to the agent in it, so an author naming the one the work is about first is saying something a reader can act on. AND THE WORKING DIRECTORY BECOMES THE FLIGHT'S OWN, with the repositories below it. It was the FIRST tree, which put an agent inside a checkout and left every other tree the flight had cloned unreachable and unmentioned. This moves the ground under flights that work today - an agent that used to start inside its checkout now starts above it - and what keeps that from being a regression is that the prompt, and the hand-flown session's announcement, now name each repository AND the directory it is in. THOSE DIRECTORIES ARE HASHES: WorkingTreeRoot fingerprints each slug deliberately, because a slug is "never a directory name", so an agent at the root sees sixteen hex characters per repository and can derive neither from the other. Naming both halves is not a nicety here - without it the move makes things worse.

A FLIGHT'S FACTS ARE READABLE. A flight records nine facts and a story shows one: two of the thirteen kinds reach it - a loop's outcome and its question - and the outcome's reason is cut where it is produced, to the first paragraph or 280 characters, on the argument that the row somebody reads first has to stay short. That argument is right, and what it left behind had no reader at all: the manifest measured for each tree, the provenance naming which commit of which repository was used, the digest extracted from a transcript precisely so somebody away from the runner could read it, and the proposal a triage or scoring flight exists to make. WHAT THAT COSTS IS THE ONE SEPARATION THIS CONTRACT IS FOR. The single visible line of a scoring flight is the agent's own prose - "Scored 18119 and proposed Custom.HAL = 4" - while the recorded proposal that either backs it or does not was unreachable, so a flight that claimed a score and recorded none read exactly like one that did. Everything else here works to keep what an agent SAYS apart from what a machine MEASURED. THE STORED ENVELOPE CROSSES, NOT A SUMMARY. FactEnvelope is already pinned and in the vocabulary because a runner ships it, so this read adds a container and a wrapper and nothing else; a summary would be a second projection of one thing, and the half a reader wants is the half a summary drops - which paths a manifest names, which fields a proposal sets, which commit a tree was at. Handing over the envelope is safe because the control plane's own rule says disposition decides the BUDGET an item is held against and not what is stored: the payload is serialized whole either way. AND THE DISPOSITION TRAVELS WITH EACH FACT, carried rather than derived - the table mapping a kind to inline, digest or reference has one owner and is not reachable from this assembly, and it is the answer to why one row has no content. THE TRANSCRIPT STAYS WHERE IT IS: it is a reference by kind, so what crosses is a hash, a size, a media type and a locator, and the bytes remain on the machine that produced them. Dereferencing is a capability this platform does not have and this read does not add one - what it does add is the first way to SEE that locator, which the truncated reason has been pointing at with no route to it. A third read beside the log and the story, and the only one of the three whose contents a customer audits: the log is what the control plane did to a flight, the story folds that for a reader, and this is what the runner shipped.

A DESTINATION NAMES ITS BRANCH. `gg/GG-118` was every branch this platform had ever made, because DestinationBranch.For took the flight number and nothing else - so a team whose convention puts the ticket in the ref had no way to say so, and a branch a person cannot read back to a backlog item is one they match up by hand. Destination.Branch is a template over {flight} and {ticket}. THE TAIL ONLY, AND THE PREFIX IS NOT THE AUTHOR'S TO CHOOSE: `gg/` is how this platform recognises its own branches - IsOurs is what cleanup reads and IsHandoff tells work kept for a takeover from work offered for merge - so an envelope that could write the prefix could write one neither predicate sees, and a remote would quietly accumulate refs nothing will ever delete. THE FLIGHT NUMBER IS REQUIRED IN IT, for a collision rather than for tidiness: two flights on one ticket is the ordinary case (a rerun after a halt is exactly that) and without the number the second push is either refused as an existing branch or overwrites the first - the same argument ForHandoff already makes one case over. A PART WITH NOTHING TO FILL IT TAKES ITS SEPARATORS WITH IT, so a flight opened from a sentence lands on `gg/GG-118` rather than `gg/-GG-118` and is not refused for a formatting choice somebody else made. Validate refuses the rest where the envelope is written - a template with no {flight}, one that spells the prefix itself, and a placeholder nothing fills, which is what somebody writes who has read another tool's documentation. EXEMPT FROM COMPOSITION on Destination.Kind's terms: every other member of that record is a bound that narrows, a name is not one, and intersecting two of them produces neither. A MEMBER AND NOT A VALUE, so an envelope written before it keeps meaning what it meant - null is the branch this platform has always made.

AN AGENT PROPOSES ITS OWN LANDING. A title cut out of prose is not one the agent chose: the landing composes one from the loop's closing account, and the rung below that was an obligation verdict written for an audit trail - pull request 8629 was called "GG-118: Destination 'pull-request' requires 'in-scope', and it holds." LoopMoves.propose-landing grants a tool on this platform's own server; LandingProposal is what an agent states through it, and landing.proposal records it. A MOVE, A TOOL AND A FACT, which is this project's one idiom for a deliberate statement - the alternative considered first was a convention inside the closing summary, and this repository already has the evidence against it: a CONSIDERED: line has been asked for in an airspace document for weeks, is cut by the reason's own first-paragraph rule before it reaches a fact, and is read by nothing on either side. RECORD-ONLY, more plainly than the work-item proposal beside it: a proposal asks that somebody else's backlog change, this asks what to call a pull request that may never be opened, and admission can still refuse the whole landing. THE TITLE IS REQUIRED, ONE LINE AND BOUNDED, REFUSED RATHER THAN TRIMMED - a silent truncation is a title the agent did not write appearing under its name, and it can read a refusal and shorten it. The description is optional on Target's terms: absent is a real answer, and a description an agent was told to write anyway is padding under somebody's name. NOT CALLED `body`, because FactManifestTests refuses that word on a fact type - a member named for content is one that will hold it - and `description` is what the provider's own create body calls the field. Destination.title and Destination.description are the instruction a person writes for whoever does the work, beside branch: and for its reason, refused on a kind that opens no proposal. LeaseLoop.landing carries them to the agent, because a document nothing renders into a lease is a policy nobody is told about - the omission that shipped twice in this product, one member apart, in the same method. Fact vocabulary 0.31.0 with it.

The board's endings become a closed vocabulary. `NominationEndings` names the six ways a nomination stops standing - opened, superseded, withdrawn, declined, refused, lapsed - and `NominationStates.Standing` names the one live value beside it. ADR-0022 section 2, and the shape is `FlightStates`' one noun earlier in a flight's life: a closed set because the only safe response to a word a reader does not know is to refuse it, and a seventh ending is therefore a version event rather than a value quietly appearing. SIX RATHER THAN THREE, BECAUSE WHO ENDED IT IS THE PART WORTH READING. A person asking why there is no flight for something is asking which of six things happened; a vocabulary that answered only 'it ended' would send them to the sentence to parse it back out. The vault already holds this line one noun over - `grounded` is not `withdrawn` - and the two vocabularies deliberately share exactly one word, `withdrawn`, which means the same thing in both: the question ceased to apply. STANDING IS SEPARATE FROM THE ENDINGS AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. It is the ABSENCE of an ending rather than one of them, so it lives in its own type; a single enumeration holding both would let a row be recorded as having ended in the state that means it has not, which is the defect `FlightStates` keeps `open` and `unknown` out of its `Exits` to avoid. AND IT COSTS A VERSION ONLY BECAUSE IT DECLARES ITS LEDGER. The consts alone moved no fingerprint - the surface was unchanged with the type present and undeclared, which is exactly the hole `Every_closed_vocabulary_declares_a_fingerprint` exists to close: a closed vocabulary in NEITHER ledger is one where a value can be added and no number moves. `[VocabularyOf(Contract)]` puts it in the wire ledger rather than the fact one, for `FlightStates`' reason: an ending is decided control-plane-side by the board and travels outward to whoever reads it, and no runner ships one inside a fact. So a value added here changes what the wire can say and never what a measurement can. RENUMBERED FROM 0.164.0 AND THE FINGERPRINT WAS RECOMPUTED RATHER THAN CARRIED. This was written as 0.164.0 and `An agent proposes its own landing` took that number first, so the rebase renumbered it - and the hash could not come with it. That commit moved the wire surface, so the surface this vocabulary is declared against is a function of both changes and not of mine alone; copying the old hash forward would have recorded a fingerprint no build ever produces, which is the one thing this ledger exists to make impossible. Recomputed after the rebase, against main.

The board gets a read surface. `NominationSummary` is one nomination as the board shows it, `BoardPage` is what the read answers with, and `GET /v1/board` is declared on the Developer audience with the session header and no runner one. Slice thirty-seven, S37.1-05. A NOMINATION IS NOT A FLIGHT AND THE SUMMARY DOES NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE. It is keyed on the nomination; the flight is a NULLABLE member, absent for every row that has not opened one - which is the whole state a board exists to render. A summary keyed on a flight would have nothing to say about most of what a person reads, which is the defect QueueRow has on the console side and the reason that criterion was rewritten. THE PAGE SAYS WHETHER IT SHOWED THE ENDED ROWS, because a reader cannot infer it. A page of standing rows and a page that happens to contain no ended ones look identical, and somebody reading 'nothing was declined' off the second would be reading a filter rather than a fact - the same reason `envelope-version: none` is written rather than left absent. DEVELOPER AUDIENCE, ON THE ARGUMENT THE FLIGHT LIST ALREADY MAKES, and with more force. A runner able to read the flight list could enumerate a tenant's work from a credential meant only to let it hold one lease at a time; the board is that list one step earlier and includes what nobody has decided about yet. The test asserts the session header present AND the runner header absent, because a required header nobody checks for is a control somebody believes they have. /v1/board JOINS GovernedPrefixes, so nothing may be served under it that is not declared here. A route under an ungoverned prefix is one anybody may add to without this repository being asked. TWO FINGERPRINTS MOVED AND ONLY ONE IS A VERSION. The endpoint fingerprint moves for the route; the wire surface moves for the two types. Recorded together because they were one change.

A flight's story can say it nominated. `StoryKinds.Nominated` is the mirror of `opened-by-admission` on the other flight: that one says a flight exists because of somebody else's classification, and this says a flight made one. IT NAMES THE KIND AND WHAT BECAME OF THE ASKING, and neither names the other flight. No field on either points at the other - the nomination row is what relates them and it points forward only - so a sentence carrying a flight number here would be the convenient reference ADR-0019 section 1 refuses, arriving as prose. WORKED RATHER THAN CREATED, though its mirror is Created. A flight is opened by admission at its beginning; a flight NOMINATES after its loop has done the work that decided what to ask for, which is the stage the loop's own entries already sit in. THE BILL WAS THREE PLACES AND TWO GUARDS FOUND THE LAST TWO. A story kind costs the constant, a FlightStories.Sentence arm, a Stories stage arm, and an entry in StoryKinds.All - and the sweep that refuses an unlisted value put it plainly: a value declared but never listed is invisible to the fingerprint that exists to notice new values, which is how a stale working copy reached production and threw. WHY IT IS HERE AT ALL: good-grief's flight log gains a `nominated` row, and StoryKindClosureTests refuses a log kind the contract has not declared because FlightStory.Sentence throws on a kind it does not know - so an undeclared one makes every story of that flight throw rather than merely missing a line.

A flight destination says HOW it opens. `Destination.OpensAs` is `auto` or `gated`, and `DestinationOpening` is the closed pair with the one reader that decides what absent means. Slice thirty-seven, S37.3-01 and S37.3-02. A SECOND BOUND BESIDE THE MENU, ANSWERING A DIFFERENT QUESTION. `opens:` says WHICH work kinds a nomination may name; this says whether one that named a permitted kind becomes a flight without anybody seeing it. A menu of one kind that opens unattended is a narrower grant than a menu of six a person looks at first, and a tenant that could only set the menu could not express either. ABSENT MEANS `auto`, AND THAT IS AN EXCEPTION TO THE RULE THIS VAULT HAS REACHED FIVE TIMES - a line that can be dropped is a constraint that can be dropped silently. It holds here because absent is not a dropped constraint: opening on admission is the only behaviour a flight destination has ever had, so silence means what it has always meant, and `gated` is the word that ADDS one. Writing `gated` over silence therefore reads as the same tightening as writing it over `auto`, or the comparator would make the safest edit in the document the expensive one. COMPOSES BY `and`, WHICH IS EXACTLY THE OPERATOR ITS SEMANTICS WANT: a two-point order where any layer may force the tight value and none may force the loose one. `gated` is tight, so a narrowing may put a person in front of an opening and no layer may take one away - `preserve-unadmitted`'s rule with a different pair of words. The direction arm is written BY HAND, because an operator in the composition table is not a direction rule, which is how `accepts:` once shipped able to be narrowed with no gate. REFUSED ON ANY OTHER KIND and on any third word, on `opens:`' terms: nothing else opens a flight, and a mode nothing implements is a destination parsing into behaviour nobody wrote. Absent stays absent through parse and render, so `envelope show` after `envelope apply` puts no line into a tenant's document that nobody wrote. THE BILL WAS NINE PLACES AND SIX GUARDS FOUND SEVEN OF THEM: the member, the two validations, a parse arm, a render arm, a hand-written direction arm, a Composes operator (a field with none 'would compose by accident'), a VocabularyOf ledger, a DirectionCoverageTests case - because 'a composed field nobody moves is a field the comparator may not read' - an EnvelopeModelRoundTripTests entry, a line in the guidance the tool server reads out (a key a document may carry that 'nothing tells an agent' exists), and the member name in ProtocolSurface.JsonMembers. The Protocol table in slice thirty-seven budgeted five for a new envelope member; nine is the number, and the four it missed were all found by guards rather than by review.

The board gets a decision door. `POST /v1/board/{id}/decisions` takes a `NominationDecision`, and `NominationDecisions` is the pair of endings a person may cause. Slice thirty-seven, S37.3-04 and S37.3-05. A SUB-RESOURCE, THE WAY A FLIGHT'S DECISIONS ARE. `/v1/flights/{ref}/decisions` is how somebody answers a gate and this is the same act one noun earlier, so it is spelled the same way rather than as a pair of verb-suffixed routes - the only `:verb` path in the surface is `/v1/leases:claim`, which takes no parameter. THE OUTCOME IS AN ENDING RATHER THAN A WORD OF ITS OWN. Opening ends a row `opened` and declining ends it `declined`, so the door speaks the vocabulary the row records. A second set of words for the same two states would be two spellings to keep agreeing, and the day they stop is the day a door produces something no row can carry. AND A PERSON MAY CAUSE ONLY THOSE TWO. Superseding is the board's, withdrawal is the world's, lapsing is the clock's and refusal is the rules' - a door accepting one of those would let somebody record that the clock did what they did. Both halves are asserted, because a list that only forbade the bad words would pass on a seventh nobody thought of. DEVELOPER AUDIENCE AND THE SESSION HEADER, NEVER A RUNNER'S: a runner able to answer a nomination could decide the work it is about to be handed, which is the containment property the platform rests on. Asserted as the session header present AND the runner header absent, because a required header nobody checks for is a control somebody believes they have. 202 AND NO BODY on ADR-0012, and 409 for a row somebody already answered - being told it is history is a different answer from being refused. TWO FINGERPRINTS MOVED AND ONLY ONE IS A VERSION: the endpoint fingerprint for the route, the wire surface for the type. Recorded together because they were one change.

A runner credential can be renewed. `RunnerCredentialRenewed` carries one member - the new expiry - and `POST /v1/runner/renewal` is declared on the Runner audience with the runner header. WHY A DESIGN STANCE MOVED: `gg runner maintain` refused on a pool host with "a pool host runs on its own runner token, which lasts thirty days and cannot be renewed - so a person signs in once to mint a new one", which means the one process whose job is keeping a pool warm with nobody present stops every thirty days and waits to be visited, and every environment downstream of it goes cold. WHAT STAYS A PERSON'S ACT IS REGISTRATION, AND RENEWAL DOES NOT TOUCH IT: the ask is authorized by the credential being renewed, so revoking or retiring ends it at once - the credential that would ask is the one that was taken away - and a runner dark past its expiry cannot ask at all, so a machine that stopped still needs a person. Nothing can be minted from nothing. NO ID IN THE PATH, on /v1/runner/hello's precedent: the runner header names who is asking, and a path id would offer a runner the chance to name somebody else's, which is a 404 to write and a fleet to enumerate. THE TOKEN DOES NOT CHANGE AND IS NOT IN THE RESPONSE. Only the expiry moves, so nothing secret crosses on the way back and a runner that fails to record the answer has lost a date rather than its identity; rotation would put the one thing a runner cannot re-obtain on the wire and make a failed disk write the end of the machine. 409 IS THE MEMBER, and it is a status rather than a 403 because it is settled rather than a misconfiguration: a pool member's twelve hours are the container boundary - "reset is only a boundary if the credential dies with the container" - and a member that renewed itself would erase it. The runner does not decide its own eligibility; it asks, and carries on from a refusal.

A board row says what it is about. `NominationSummary.IntentKey` carries the uri or ticket reference the nomination concerns, or nothing. Slice thirty-seven, the renderable half of S37.4-02. THE WORK KIND IS NOT A DESCRIPTION, which is what this fixes: a line reading `research-27` says which governance regime would apply and nothing about which piece of work, and a board is a list somebody scans to choose - so every renderer was printing a kind and calling it a description. The row in the control plane already recorded the key; this is the summary catching up, not a new fact. OPTIONAL, AND ABSENT MEANS UNCOUNTABLE RATHER THAN UNRECORDED. A uri or a ticket reference names something outside gg; a sentence somebody typed names nothing, so it has no key - and a hash of the words would look like the others and group nothing, which is worse than an absence because a budget keyed on it would bound each retyping separately while reading as though it bounded the work. THE KEY AND NOT THE INTENT, on the same argument that keeps the digest and the layer list off this type: a whole intent would put the text somebody typed on every line of a queue, and a thing a person scans should not be mostly provenance.

A runner says whether its agent can start, and a gate says what it is asking for. `AgentReading` on its own Runner-audience route, `POST /v1/runner/agent`, not the heartbeat, for the allowance readings' reason: a heartbeat is liveness only because a runner able to report something about itself can report it while dead, and this is a MEASUREMENT with its own MeasuredAt. No id in the path, for renewal's. STANDING, NOT STATE: a runner's state is the control plane's to derive and nothing may report it - the surface tests refuse a request member so named - and this is the agent's standing, the runner's own word for it. `needs-login` is what a maintenance incident is minted from and `ready` what recovers it; `AgentCredentialSources` says whether the credential is one gg placed (token) or one the machine's user made (machine), because only the first is gg's to revoke. The diagnosis is bounded and refused when it looks like a token: Article VIII at the door. `PendingGate.Maintenance` is a nullable `GateMaintenance` - absence is silence - because a gate cannot say what it is for through Because: an unconditional obligation's reason is the engine's fixed sentence, and a flight's name is what somebody called it. A console that offers the act clearing a runner-login gate, rather than approve or reject, has to be TOLD, and `GateMaintenanceKinds` is closed so a kind this build does not know renders as an ordinary gate. `StoryKinds.RunnerIncident` is declared because the control plane's closure test refuses a log kind this contract has not named. Measured on a live pool member: the agent answered "Not logged in" in 137 ms and the runner read an empty tree as a held bound; now it holds, beats, and says so.

An agent is logged in over the channel, and the token never crosses it. `begin-agent-login` and `finish-agent-login` join the runner-ask vocabulary, which is now five verbs on three sides rather than two: a SPAWNING verb is not a writing verb wearing a new name, and TheChannelHasAWritingVerbTests grew a third partition to say so. The runner drives its agent's own browser ceremony - `claude setup-token`, which the spike measured as wanting a terminal and printing its URL as an OSC-8 hyperlink - hands back the URL, and waits for the code a person brings from the browser. THE URL IS SAFE TO SHOW and the code is useless alone: the ceremony is PKCE with S256, so the verifier stays in the child on the runner. `AgentLoginBegun` carries started, the url, a diagnosis and when the runner gives up; `AgentLoginFinished` is `ConfiguredCredential`'s shape - locator and whether, never the value - because it is the same fact about the same file, and what differs is only that the runner minted the token rather than being handed it. Both are stripped like every other line off a machine, and the URL may not carry a line break: a URL that can is a URL that can hide a second one. CHANNEL-ONLY, asserted rather than intended: no endpoint's request, response or pending response reaches any of the four types, so there is no body a code or a token could enter on the way to a control plane. `RunnerAskBounds.MaxLoginCode` is the contract's bound so both ends refuse the same thing; a runner that trusted the length it was sent would be a runner a console could type a file into. The gate is a key of its own, `accept-agent-login`, closed by default, no variable, not offerable, and NOT opened by a member's nonce: a machine that agreed to be handed a secret has not agreed to start a program that mints one.

A repository declares what its pull requests nominate, and what that draws on. `RegisterRepositoryRequest` gains `Nominates` - a `flight` `Destination` - and `Budget`, a `NominationBudget` of flights per window. Slice thirty-eight, S38.3-01, S38.3-02 and S38.3-06. THE BOUND IS A FLIGHT DESTINATION AND NOT A MENU THAT RESEMBLES ONE: ADR-0022 section 5 says it of a watch's bound and it is reached one nominator earlier here, so `opens:`, `may-select`, `opens-as` and `requires` mean what they already mean, are validated by the rules they already have, and are reached by a narrowing through composition that already exists. A second menu-shaped member would need its own validation, its own direction arms and its own way to be reached - three places for two spellings to stop agreeing. THE REPOSITORY CARRIES BOTH BECAUSE IT IS THE NOMINATOR: section 5 lists a watch's budget among its BOUNDS, beside rate and active hours, rather than among its BOUND, which is the destination - so a budget belongs to whoever nominates, and a pull request's nominator is the repository it is in. ABSENT IS TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR AND IS STATED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED PAST: every repository registered before this has no bound and nominates an un-kinded flight under the tenant's current envelope, so a declared bound is the word that ADDS a constraint - the exception `opens-as` made, for its reason. ZERO IS REFUSED RATHER THAN READ AS UNBOUNDED, because absent already means unbounded and zero would mean a repository that may nominate nothing at all - something somebody might mean, and so something that must not be reachable by leaving a number out. AND TWO DIRECTION ARMS EXIST FOR WHAT A COMPARATOR GETS WRONG BY OMISSION: removing a budget is a widening, because absent means unbounded and two numbers cannot be compared when one is not there; and a window lengthened for the same count is a TIGHTENING while a shortened one is a widening, because the rate bounds a loop and the numerator does not. `DestinationOpening.Refused` is extracted so the envelope's own destination loop and a bound written outside one are validated by the same three sentences rather than by two copies of them.

A gated nomination says why, when nothing authored the gate. `NominationSummary.gatedBecause` is null for `opens-as: gated` - a person put in front of an opening on purpose, whose reason is the destination somebody wrote - and carries a sentence when arithmetic reached the same word. A repository's nomination budget is the first thing that can: it runs out, and the row stands gated with the story of what this intent has already spent inside the window and how those nominations ended. NOT A THIRD MODE WORD, and the reason is at the registration door: `DestinationOpening` reads two words and refuses a third, which `ARepositoryDeclaresWhatItNominatesTests` holds, so a third would make `opens-as: exhausted` an authorable value in a destination document. Nobody authors exhaustion. The discriminator is the member's PRESENCE, which is a structural read rather than a reader parsing prose to tell two gates apart - and a sentence rather than a number because a bare count says the budget is gone and not whether the spending was productive, which is the question somebody answering the row is actually holding.

A registration reads back what it nominates. `RepositoryRegistered` gains `nominates` and `budget`, the two members 0.174.0 put on the request and the 201 body echoed neither of - so `gg airspace repositories` can show what a repository's pull requests may open and how often, and the only way to learn it stops being pushing a commit and watching. It is this record's own rule at its sharpest: a declaration a tenant can write and cannot read back is one they cannot check, and this pair decides what a webhook nobody was watching may do. BOTH NULLABLE, on `narrowings`' asymmetry rather than `credential`'s - absent and declared are different facts here, unbounded versus bounded, so the absence survives as an absence and every registration made before 0.174.0 reads back honestly. The same type in both directions rather than a listing-shaped paraphrase, because two spellings of one governance control stop agreeing the first time either moves.

A MEMBER NAMES THE MACHINE THAT RUNS IT. RunnerSummary gains HostRunnerId, null on everything that is not a pool member, so a fleet can be read as the shape it is rather than as one flat list. A MEMBER IS A RUNNER WITHOUT BEING A PEER: it beats, it holds a credential, it takes one by send, and a maintenance ask can name it - but a maintainer on somebody's host created it and it dies with the pool, so three machines listed under fifteen members is a list nobody can use. NOTHING THE CLIENT ALREADY RECEIVES SUPPLIES THE LINK, which is why this had to be a field rather than a rendering: the label cannot carry it, since gg-pool-ui-1 says nothing about which machine warmed it, and the pool ledger carries no runner at all. FOUND BY DEBUGGING A GATE NOBODY COULD ANSWER - members reached no listing, so a maintenance ask named a machine whose owner's every tool refused it, `gg credential send` included, which is the command the member's own logs tell them to run. OMITTED WHEN NULL, so a control plane that has not learned this sends the body it has always sent and the two are indistinguishable to any reader - which is what lets the field ship before the control plane fills it.

A WATCH IS A FIFTH ROLE. ADR-0022 section 5's document arrives: `WatchDocument` with a shape, a trigger, a host and credential REFERENCE, a filter, a skill path at a ref, a mapping, a bound and bounds - plus `WatchTrigger`, `WatchMapping` and `WatchBounds`, and `Roles.Watch` with a `watches/` directory. The document never contains a procedure: the skill is a path read at a ref, the credential is a locator the runner resolves into a server's environment, and there is no member a script can travel in - the script is the repository's, landed by a crystalize flight in slice forty. THE MAPPING IS THREE FIELDS and the exclusions are the argument: a nomination carries more, but the work kind comes from the bound's `opens:`, the mode from its `opens-as`, and the reason and note from the executor; `environment` and `repository` are left out because nothing on this path selects, there being no classifier in front of a watch. THE BOUND IS REQUIRED HERE where a repository's is optional - a repository existed before the member so absent had to mean today's behaviour, while nothing else tells a sweep what kind to nominate. `NominationBounds` now holds the two leaf rules both doors share, so the same malformed bound comes back as the same sentence at a watch and at a repository rather than from two validators that agree today. `PullPoints` was closed at one and gains `control-plane` and `forge-scheduler`, legal for a watch and refused for a STRATEGY, because a pool the control plane performs is a pool nothing warms. And `EnvelopeText` gained a watch renderer with the destination block EXTRACTED rather than copied, on `ObligationBlock`'s precedent: two emitters with two destination blocks would disagree about the canonical form the day one gained a member.

A WATCH HAS A DOOR OF ITS OWN. PUT, GET one and GET all under /v1/airspace/watches, on the strategy door's shape one document class over, with `WatchState` and `WatchList` as the answers - the strategy state's shape with one member renamed, so a reader that holds one already knows how to hold the other. The document had already landed on the control plane's stream with no route in front of it, which is a port nothing calls. A door of its own rather than the named-envelope door, because the body is a different document class and the request type should say which rather than leave the server a union to guess at. PUT DECLARES 202, AND THAT IS A PROMISE: a widening watch is diverted to the gate rather than refused, so whichever side pins this must serve the diversion and the re-apply that follows it.

A RUNNER NAMES ITS MACHINE. RunnerRegistrationRequest and RunnerSummary each gain an optional Machine. A machine runs several runners - the resident that takes flights, a maintainer per pool, an attended runner started by hand - and each is its own registration, so nothing on the wire said they share a host. THE LABEL ONLY IMPLIED IT: every gg registration derives its label from the host name, vmlinux001 and vmlinux001:maintain alike, so the machine was known at registration and never sent, and parsing it back out would promote a string convention to an identity. FOUND BY A PERSON READING THE FLEET: members were nested under the runner attesting their pool, which on vmlinux001 is the maintainer - a registration that never beats and reads as offline - so two healthy members sat under a dead-looking parent instead of under the machine. A member's machine is its maintainer's, since a member's own label names its pool slot and not its host. OPTIONAL BOTH WAYS: an older client sends no machine and must still register, and an older control plane records none, so the key is omitted when null and either side's wire is unchanged.

A WATCH NAMES WHAT IT READS, AND CHANGING THAT IS REVIEWED. `WatchDocument.Repository` - a registry name, required - says which registered repository the skill path is in. `Skill` was 'a path in the repository' and ADR-0022 section 5 says 'the repository it references', but the document referenced none, so whatever fetched the skill would have had to guess whose tree to read. The control plane fetches it (ADR-0018 section 5, one noun over), and a registered repository is one somebody declared through a gate with a forge binding to reach it by. AND `WatchDirection` NOW WIDENS ON ANY CHANGE to the repository, skill, ref, host, credential, shape, pull point or any of the three mapping fields. It compared the bound, the filter, the period and the bounds and nothing a watch reads or reaches, so a ref moved to a branch nobody reviewed applied ungated - which defeats the member whose purpose is 'so what ran is what somebody reviewed'. Each is the filter's argument: none has an order this side can compute, so equality is the only comparison and a change is reviewed. One arm and one sentence per member. A longer period, lower bounds and a narrower bound remain ungated.

A SWEEP IS A SERVED ACTION. Slice thirty-nine step 2, on the pools surface's shape and for its reason: a sweep has no flight, so the lease-welded fact pipeline cannot carry it. GET /v1/watches/{name}/actions is the pull point - serving is the claim, so two runners polling one watch run one sweep, and nothing decided is an empty list. POST /v1/watches/{name}/attestations is the report, 202 because it is a command and 400 because `WatchAttestation.Validate` refuses on both sides. /v1/watches is governed from its first route. `WatchAction` carries the watch whole at the version it was decided under, the executor, and either a `WatchSkill` or a diagnosis - never both, never neither - so a skill the control plane could not read still reaches a person as an unreachable sweep rather than a row nobody serves. THE SKILL CARRIES A CUSTOMER'S WORDS ONE WAY: ADR-0023 section 1 has the control plane fetch it and hand it over, and the commit and digest travel beside it because those are all the control plane keeps (PolicyFile's rule; docs/patterns.md rule 8 on the private side). `WatchAttestation` is `swept` or `unreachable`; an empty sweep is valid, because found-nothing is a result and silence is a fault; an unreachable sweep says why and reports nothing seen; a good pass carries no diagnosis. `WatchSighting` is a subject, a version and an optional intent key, each bounded, with at most 1000 per report - the limits are what keep a work item's text from arriving in a store under an identity's name, and no report member is named for a secret or for text. ONE EXECUTOR, `instructions`: ADR-0023's script executor arrives with the crystalize flight that writes one, and declaring it first would be a word nothing performs.

A RUNNER STATES ITS MACHINE AFTER THE FACT. RunnerMachineOffer and POST /v1/runner/machine, for RunnerKeyOffer's reason one fact over: registration is read-or-register, so a runner with a stored credential never registers again, and a machine added to registration at 0.180.0 reached only runners registered from then on. The resident and the maintainer on a long-lived host - exactly the two a person wants members grouped under - would otherwise stay machineless for as long as their credentials last. RUNNER AUDIENCE WITH NO ID IN THE PATH, on the agent reading's reason: the credential names the runner, and a body or path that could name one would let a runner speak for another. 204 AND NO 409, which is where it parts from the key offer: consoles pinned the first key, so a different one is a substitution, but a machine is a display grouping nothing authorizes on and a runner moved to another host simply says so.

THE RUNNER READS THE SKILL, AT A COMMIT THE CONTROL PLANE PINS. Decided 2026-09-16 by the owner, amending 0.182.0. The control plane's forge surface reads exactly one thing from a customer's repository - a declared narrowings directory - and no code, and ADR-0023's first draft had the control plane fetching a watch's skill and later its script past both; 0.182.0 put that on the wire as `WatchSkill.Content`. So `WatchSkill` is gone and `WatchAction.SkillCommit` replaces `Skill`: the control plane resolves the watch's ref to a commit, a metadata call it already makes, and the runner reads the skill there with the customer's credential. A commit or a diagnosis, never both and never neither, and a commit is forty or sixty-four hex digits - a ref is refused, because a pin that moves pins nothing. `WatchAttestation.SkillSha` carries the digest of what the sweep followed, on the runner's word since nothing else read the file: required on a good pass, optional on an unreachable one, which may never have read the skill. Nothing on the wire has anywhere to put a skill's words, and a test holds that structurally. No control plane pinned 0.182.0, so nothing served the removed member.

A SWEEP CARRIES WHAT ITS EXECUTOR NOMINATED. Decided 2026-09-16 by the owner, reversing slice thirty-nine's rule 7 (the runner reports, the control plane nominates): "the sweep runs on a runner - i think the agent and/or script should be doing that. that way it can be dynamic if necessary." So `WatchAttestation.Saw` becomes `Nominated`, and `WatchSighting` becomes `SweepNomination` - keeping its pinned id, because a rename must not change the wire identity - with the three members that make a nomination: the kind the executor chose (optional; a menu of one names it, and a menu of more with no choice is the board's refusal to write), its reason (required) and a note, bounded at FlightNomination's own measured lengths. The report carries at most 256, TrackerAdmission's number for its reason. The board still decides each one, rule by rule. A sweep's nominations travel here rather than as facts because a sweep has no flight and the fact pipeline is lease-welded. AND `WatchAction.Moves`: the owner accepted that every sweep's tools are a shipped `sweep` work kind's, composed control-plane-side and handed over, since a sweep has no lease to carry an envelope and a watch has no moves of its own. An unknown move is refused; an empty list is a tenant's tightening. No control plane has recorded a sighting, so nothing read the renamed member.

A MAINTAINER READS AS MAINTAINING. RunnerStates gains `maintaining`: not beating, and reporting on a pool recently. vmlinux001:maintain read `offline, never seen` while it reported every five seconds, because state was derived from heartbeats alone and a maintainer sends none - a heartbeat is an offer to take work, and having it beat would have made it read `idle`, a promise it never keeps. A STATE, WHERE PARKING WAS NOT: ARunnerCanBeParkedTests keeps parking beside the state because state says what a runner is doing and parking is policy; maintaining a pool is what this runner is doing, and the choice was put to a person. ALIVE IS NOT REACHABLE: an introduction is picked up on a heartbeat, so nothing can be handed to a maintaining runner, and gg refuses watch, credential and agent login for one before minting anything. RunnerSummary.LastHeartbeatAt is documented as last heard from - for a runner that reports on a pool, the later of its heartbeat and its latest report - so a maintainer has a last-seen; display only. AN OLDER gg prints the word as it arrives and neither tints nor refuses it: its checks name `offline`, so a watch or a send aimed at a maintainer there waits out an introduction and says it was not reached.

A SWEEP SAYS WHICH REPOSITORY ITS SKILL IS IN. 0.184.0 gave a served sweep `SkillCommit` and nothing else, while the watch names its repository by the tenant's registry name - and a runner's fetch is keyed by provider and slug, so the runner held a commit and no way to reach the repository it is in. `WatchAction.Skill` replaces `SkillCommit` as a `LeaseRepoRef`, the coordinate type the runner's VCS port already takes, with the commit as its `PinnedRef`. The control plane resolves the registry name when it serves the sweep. The rules carry over: a pin or a diagnosis, never both and never neither; a pin is a commit of forty or sixty-four hex digits; and a blank provider or slug is refused. No control plane has served a sweep, so nothing read the removed member.

A WATCH SAYS HOW IT IS DOING. S39.6-01 wants, per watch, the executor in force, the cost per window and the newest attestation, and none of the three is in the document - so `WatchStanding` and `WatchStandingList` carry them on a read of their own, GET /v1/airspace/watch-standings. NOT MEMBERS ON `WatchState`: that is the type `gg airspace pull` writes a working copy from, and a working copy exists to be diffed against what somebody wrote - liveness members there would change those files on every pull. THE EXECUTOR IS REPORTED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED, read from the newest decided sweep: every sweep today carries `instructions` and ADR-0023's script executor arrives later, so a member answering the shipped word by construction would be wrong the day the second one lands with nothing having changed. A watch that never swept has none, said as null. `QuietSince` is the liveness answer and null is healthy - it is not the same as a recent `LastHeardAt`, because a watch that has never swept has no last-heard and can still be quiet, measured from when it was applied. The cost is the number the budget compares against, beside the bound itself so a reader sees a scale rather than a bare count; unbounded reports the count and no bound, because unbounded is a state. ONE route and a hyphenated path: `/v1/airspace/watches/standings` would shadow a watch somebody named `standings`.

A POOL ROLLS ONTO ITS PIN. `PoolActions` gains `roll`, classified an outward act: make every member current with the strategy's pinned image, destroying and recreating the ones made from something it no longer names. Measured on vmlinux001 on 2026-09-17 - an image was built, pushed and named by an applied strategy, and three hours later one pool ran three different images, because the decider decides an act only while the pool is BELOW its warm target and `verify`, the only action a full pool ever gets, compares no images at all. A running member never converged, and growing the pool by one was the only way to get a member onto a new image - which rides a widening gate and needs a person. NOT A WIDER `refresh`: refresh is how a pool GROWS, one member per decision with a hold-off tuned to that pace and only under the warm ceiling, while a roll adds nobody and must act AT the ceiling, which is the state a pool sits in while its members go stale. WHOLE-POOL, because which members drifted is knowable only where the containers are, by comparing what each says it was made FROM against the pin: a roll converging one member would leave the rest waiting on a decision made from a count the control plane cannot measure. An older control plane decides no rolls, and an older runner answers one it is served with "'roll' is not an action this runner knows how to take" - a failed attestation naming the word, which is the arm that destroys nothing.

THE RUNNER RESOLVES ITS SKILL'S REF, decided 2026-09-17 by the owner, amending rule 16: "the runners should be doing the work not the control plane". `WatchAction.Skill.PinnedRef` carried the commit the control plane had resolved and now carries the watch's REF, and `WatchAttestation` gains `SkillCommit` - what the runner landed on. WHAT THIS GIVES UP is stated rather than discovered: the refusal this removes said "a branch or a tag moves, and a pin that moves pins nothing", and that is still true - two sweeps of one decided action can read different skills if the branch moved between them. What replaces the guarantee is a RECORD: the commit is reported beside the blob digest, so what ran is answerable afterwards rather than fixed beforehand, and a good pass that will not name one is refused. WHAT IT BUYS is reach: the runner already holds the credential and clones the repository either way, and `CloneOutcome.HeadCommit` already carries the commit - so nothing new computes it, and the control plane stops needing forge reach per tenant for this path. That is what blocked a watch whose skill is in a repository on a forge this system has no binding shape for, where the refusal a person read named another forge's idea of an installation. RULE 19 IS UNTOUCHED - the control plane still resolves the repository NAME to a provider and a slug, because the registry lives there and the machine that fetches holds none. A commit is still accepted in the ref slot, so a caller holding one may hand it over.

A RESIDENT RUNNER CLAIMS A SWEEP WITHOUT NAMING A WATCH. POST /v1/runner/sweeps/claim, carrying `SweepClaim` - the (host, credential locator) pairs this runner can reach - and answering with the `WatchActionList` the named pull already answers with. The owner, running slice thirty-nine's walk: "today a watch sweeps only while someone keeps that process running - we need to have the runner automatically check." The only pull was GET /v1/watches/{name}/actions, scoped to one watch, so something had to supply the name and what did was a person at a shell running `gg runner sweep`; a watch whose document says `pull-point: resident-runner` was pulled by no resident runner. NAMES NO WATCH because a flight claim names no flight - the runner asks and the control plane matches. THE PAIRS because rule 18 presents a credential only where the operator declared the pair, and a runner that claimed a sweep it could not serve would attest a false unreachable; the control plane serves only a watch naming one of them. ON THE CLAIM, not the heartbeat: labels ride the heartbeat because flights are routed before anybody asks, while a sweep is pulled - so the pairs travel with the pull that uses them, are never stored, and cannot go stale. A locator is a reference rather than a secret, and the watch document carries the same one. A claim that can reach nothing is refused rather than answered empty: that is a runner's mistake, and an empty answer would read as a quiet period.

A WATCH SAYS WHEN IT SWEEPS NEXT. `WatchStanding` gains `NextSweepAt` and `NextSweepSaid`, because the board was asked when the next run is and no reader can work it out. The schedule is timed between two DECISIONS - so a runner's pace never stretches it and its clock never shortens it - and it is held back by a latch while a sweep has not reported, and by the watch's active hours. A standing carries none of those: it has `LastHeardAt`, which is when a sweep REPORTED, one sweep's duration after the decision the period is measured from. So a console computing a next run from what it already had would print a number that disagrees with the planner exactly when somebody is asking why nothing has run. TWO MEMBERS, because a time and a reason are different answers: a reason with no time is a watch nothing will ever pull - an unperformed pull point, a period that does not read as a duration - and a blank there would read as "soon". A time in the past is not stale; it means decided and waiting for a runner to take it.

A LOOP MAY DECLARE THAT IT IS UNBOUNDED. `LoopMoves` gains `anything`: the envelope saying it will not bound this agent at all. The owner asked for an option to let the agent be dangerous, and before this there were two ways to get there and both were worse than saying so - declare `run-tests` and reach the rest through Bash, which is a bound defeated rather than declined; or turn the bound off on the machine, which no envelope names, no probe contradicts and no fact records. A VALUE AND NOT A FIELD, which is the whole reason it costs a version: the only safe response to an unknown value in a closed vocabulary is to halt, so an added value breaks every prior reader by design - while the same statement as a member (`unbounded: true`) would be IGNORED by a reader that predates it, which would believe the flight was bounded. The dangerous option has to arrive through the door that halts. ALONE OR NOT AT ALL: `[read, anything]` is refused at authoring naming the loop, because a reader cannot tell whether `read` was meant to hold and a bound nobody can read is worse than no bound. It grants no tool - it removes `--allowedTools` and passes the agent binary's own bypass flag - so asking which tool it maps to throws rather than answering with the move's spelling. Classified record-only like everything else, for run-tests' reason stated at its widest: an outward act no probe can confirm is refused at authoring, so the honest-looking classification would make the value undeclarable, which is the machine-level switch it was minted to replace. A SWEEP MAY NOT DECLARE IT - a sweep is decided by a schedule and performed with nobody looking. TWO MEANINGS MOVE WITHOUT A MEMBER MOVING: `MoveEnforcements.none` crosses from a working runner for the first time (0.16.0's note said it never would), because an unbounded session is not probed and null would say UNMEASURED, which is the attended flight's weaker answer; and loop.digest's refusedMoves is empty by construction, because a refusal is a tool the envelope did not name and this envelope named them all.

A STRATEGY MAY NAME ITS RECIPE. `EnvironmentStrategy` gains `Build` (`StrategyBuild`: a repository by its registry name, a path, a ref, and optionally a Dockerfile name) and `BuiltFrom` (`StrategyProvenance`: the repository, path and commit the image in force was built from). Slice forty-one, S41.1-01. A strategy pinned its image by digest and nothing said where that image came from: on the dev tenant's pool host one recipe lived in a checkout of this repository and the other in a directory no repository held, and the dev image shipped a hand-copied gg 0.1.0 for two weeks with nothing the platform held able to say so. THE DIGEST STAYS THE PIN: `image` is still the only thing a member is made from, `Validate`'s digest rule holds beside a recipe, and `build` is never read when a member is made - it says where the NEXT pin comes from. BY REFERENCE, NEVER BY CONTENT: neither record has a member a Dockerfile's text could arrive in, and `StrategyContainmentTests` now holds both to its shape and name checks. Refused at authoring: a recipe missing a part, a path that could leave the repository (`..`, absolute, a backslash), a Dockerfile that could leave the directory, and a `built-from` with no recipe, naming another recipe, or carrying a ref where a commit belongs. BOTH MEMBERS ARE ADDITIVE AND ABSENT MEANS WHAT IT DID: every strategy in force names no recipe, renders no new line, and reads back unchanged, so the first pull after this reports nothing. A CONTROL PLANE PINNED BELOW THIS REFUSES THE NEW KEYS, because it reads a strategy strictly - so it must be pinned before any `gg` writes one.

A BUILD IS A POOL ACTION. `PoolActions` gains `build`, classified an outward act; `PoolAction` gains `Recipe` (`PoolRecipe`: a `LeaseRepoRef`, a path, and an optional Dockerfile name); `PoolAttestation` gains `RecipeCommit`; and `POST /v1/airspace/strategies/{name}/builds` is declared, developer audience, answering 202 with the decided action, 404 for a strategy that names no recipe and 409 while a build stands. Slice forty-one, S41.2-01: a strategy may name its recipe since 0.194.0, and this is how a build of it is asked for and answered. OUTWARD, THOUGH IT TOUCHES NO MEMBER: the kinds table defines record-only as 'the attestation is its whole product', and a build's product is an image in a registry, pushed through a proxy allowance the scope probe must prove - which is what the decider withholds an outward act for. THE RECIPE CROSSES AS A LeaseRepoRef, the coordinate type the runner's VCS port already takes, as a sweep's skill has since 0.187.0: the control plane resolves the tenant's registry name when it decides and the name never leaves it; the ref rides as the pinned ref and the runner resolves it. A GOOD BUILD ATTESTS THE COMMIT AND THE DIGEST - the commit is a commit and never the ref, a failed build needs only its reason, and only a build may carry a recipe commit, because one on a refresh is a claim about a build that did not happen. Nothing added can carry a Dockerfile's text, and PoolAttestationTests now holds PoolRecipe and LeaseRepoRef to its shape and forbidden-name checks. AN OLDER RUNNER is handed no build - it cannot pull an action it does not know - and an older control plane decides none.

A BRANCH TEMPLATE MAY NAME THE WHOLE BRANCH. `DestinationBranch` gains `WholeBranch` (`refs/heads/`): a destination's `branch:` starting with it names the whole branch rather than the part after `gg/`, so `refs/heads/feature/{flight}-{ticket}` pushes `feature/GG-189-18493`. Asked for 2026-09-19. NO WIRE CHANGE - the surface is 0.195.0's - but a RULE both sides run moved, and the control plane names the branch at admission, so it needs this version to honour the form; below it, the form renders `gg/refs/heads/...`. OPTED INTO, NEVER INFERRED: every template in force names a tail and keeps meaning exactly that. A HANDOFF STAYS UNDER `gg/handoff/` whatever the template says, because `IsHandoff` is the one prefix product code reads. `Validate` now refuses a template naming a ref that is not a branch (`refs/tags/`, `refs/pull/`). The remark that `IsOurs` is what branch cleanup reads was false - nothing calls it - and is corrected where it appeared.

A WATCH SAYS WHOSE IT IS. `WatchDocument` gains `For`: `tenant`, absent (which means the tenant, and is what every watch before this meant), or one person spelled `<provider>:<subject>`. ADR-0024: a watch is the tenant's or one person's, and there is nothing in between, so a value that is neither is refused rather than read as the tenant. A personal watch's pull point must be `resident-runner` - it sweeps only on its person's own runners, and the control plane holds no person's credential. `PersonSpelling` is the one parser a watch's `for:` and an obligation's `approver:` both read: a colon is the claim to be a person, a bare value is a role as `platform-owner` is, and `Envelope.Validate` now refuses a human obligation whose approver claims to be a person and is not a well-formed one. SYNTAX ONLY: this repository names no identity provider, so which providers exist and what their subjects look like are the control plane's, which resolves the person to a principal and refuses one that names nobody. `WatchDirection` reports a change to `for` as its own widening, with the only way a watch changes hands - retire it and declare it again - because the control plane refuses such a version outright; absent and `tenant` are one answer and writing the default is not a change. The estate renders `for:` first and only when it was said. AN OLDER CONTROL PLANE ignores the member, so every watch it holds stays the tenant's.

A PERSON OWNS THEIR WATCH, AND NOBODY TYPES A SUBJECT. `DeclareNameRequest` gains `Personal`: a flag and never a person - the control plane binds the name to the session's principal, so nothing in a body can put a name in somebody else's hands. ADR-0024: a personal watch is its person's to own, so its name is declared with no gate. `TopologyName` gains `For`, whose name it is as a person is spelled, null for the tenant's. `WhoAmI` gains `Subject`, the person as a document names them (`<provider>:<subject>`), because that spelling is an opaque string nobody knows by heart and is only usable if gg supplies it. gg: `gg airspace name watch <name> --personal` declares the asker's own watch and writes the bound person into the watch's file when it exists and reads as a watch - keeping its `based-on:` - or says the line to write; `--personal` is refused for any role but a watch, since a personal work kind or narrowing would be one person's governance of everybody's work. `gg whoami` prints the subject when the control plane sends one and no line when it does not. AN OLDER CONTROL PLANE ignores `Personal`, so the name is declared as the tenant's, through its gate, and `For` comes back absent - so gg writes nothing it was not told.

WHOSE A RUNNER IS, APART FROM WHAT IT TAKES. ADR-0025 section 6, slice forty-three rules 4-8 and 12. `reserved_to` said both whose a runner was and that it took only that person's flights, so a person could not own a machine that still took the tenant's work and a fleet machine could not belong to the tenant and to nobody. `RunnerOwnerships` is the vocabulary: `tenant` (an admin has said nobody claims it), `open` (anybody here may claim it, for themselves) and `claimed` (one person's). `RunnerSummary` gains `Ownership`, `Owner`, `OwnerPrincipalId`, `Reserved`, `Resident` and `Profile`; `RunnerClaimRequest` (empty - the act is 'mine', and a member could only name somebody else), `RunnerOwnershipRequest` and `RunnerOwnership` are new. Doors: `POST /v1/runners/{id}/claim` (403 not ever - a tenant runner; 409 not now - somebody else's), `DELETE /v1/runners/{id}/claim` (the owner's or an admin's; ends the reservation; no 409), and `PUT /v1/runners/{id}/ownership` (an admin's, tenant and open only, 409 for a claimed runner - unclaim it first - so an owner never loses a machine without that being its own recorded act). RESERVATION'S DOORS KEEP THEIR SHAPE AND CHANGE THEIR MEANING: the owner's only, 409 'claim it first' for an unowned runner, 403 for somebody else's - including DELETE, which any developer could call before. EMPTY IS NOT OPEN: an older control plane sends no `ownership`, and gg shows nothing rather than inviting a claim with no door. Resident and profile cross now and are filled by later steps (enrollment, profiles); until then they are false and absent.

A PROFILE SAYS WHAT AN ENROLLED MACHINE IS. ADR-0025 section 2, slice forty-three rules 13-15. `FleetProfile` is a new airspace document, `fleet/<name>.yaml`, role `fleet-profile` (Roles.All moves to six): roles (`ProfileRoles`: run, maintain), an environment, an agent, forges (key=host), destinations (key=api), sweeps, and credential references. IT NAMES AND THE MACHINE RESOLVES: `Validate` refuses a path where an agent's name belongs and anything but a reference (local:, keyvault://<vault-host>/<secret>) where a credential belongs, and the refusal never repeats a value that could have been a secret. `FleetProfile.Widening` is the one comparator, in the contract so gg orders an apply by the rule the control plane applies it with: a role, forge, destination or credential added, sweeps turned on, or a changed environment or agent widens; removing any of them tightens. `FleetProfile.LabelFor` is the label a lease matches: environment=<environment>. Doors: `PUT /v1/airspace/fleet/{name}` (400 a refusal, 202 a widening diverted to the gate), `GET /v1/airspace/fleet/{name}` and `GET /v1/airspace/fleet`. `OfferedConfiguration` gains `Profile`: an offer that is a profile. Its directed keys were accepted at the profile's gate, so gg takes them without a person - only on a machine whose own file names that profile as the one it enrolled under (`enrolled-profile`, file-only, never offerable, written by enrolling). The control plane naming a profile is a claim; the file is the consent. AN OLDER CONTROL PLANE has no fleet door: gg reads a 404 on the list as no profiles, so a pull keeps working, and an offer without `Profile` is held for a person exactly as before.

A MACHINE ENROLLS ITSELF WITH A TOKEN A PERSON MINTED. ADR-0025 section 1, slice forty-three rules 17-19. `gg login` at every machine kept a person at a keyboard for each one; an enrollment token is that person's decision made once. `EnrollmentTokenRequest` names a fleet profile, a use count and an expiry - both required, the expiry at most seven days (`EnrollmentBounds.MaxLifetime`, an invitation's lifetime for a weaker thing) - and whose each machine starts as: the tenant's (an admin's to mint), open, or claimed by the minter, optionally reserved. `EnrollmentBounds.Validate` is the shape both sides refuse on; who may mint a tenant token is the session's and only the control plane's to decide. `EnrollmentTokenMinted` carries the secret once; `EnrollmentTokenSummary` and `EnrollmentTokenList` have no member it could travel in. `RunnerEnrollmentRequest` / `RunnerEnrolled`: `POST /v1/runners/enrollments` is ANONYMOUS, authorized by the token alone as `/v1/pools/members/redeem` is by its nonce, and 403 is every refusal - spent, expired, revoked or never minted - in one sentence, so a token cannot be probed. What the machine becomes (tenant, registrar, labels, ownership, profile) is the token's, never the request's. `/v1/fleet` is a new governed prefix: `POST /v1/fleet/tokens` (403 a tenant token from a non-admin, 404 a profile not in force), `GET /v1/fleet/tokens`, `POST /v1/fleet/tokens/{id}/revocation` (idempotent; enrolled machines are untouched). gg: `gg fleet enroll|tokens|revoke`; `gg runner up` redeems the token an install left beside config.json before it asks for a session, writes `enrolled-profile`, and spends the seed - and no longer needs a session at all when it holds a runner credential of its own.

A MACHINE SAYS WHAT IT LACKS. Slice forty-three rule 25, gg's half of bring-up. Only the machine can say whether a credential reference resolves or a forge answers, so it reads what it enrolled as - `GET /v1/runner/profile`, runner audience, 404 for a runner enrolled under no profile - and reports a `ReadinessReading` against that profile's name and VERSION, so a reading taken before an apply cannot close a gate the new version opened. `ReadinessKinds` is closed at three: agent (the profile names one and this machine declares another or none - its LOGIN stays `AgentReading`'s, which already opens its own gate), credential (a reference this machine cannot resolve) and forge (a host it cannot reach, by the forge's key). `ReadinessItem` names what was checked and never what a check produced. `POST /v1/runner/readiness` takes the agent reading's shape: its own route, its own measuredAt, 202 and nothing back. gg measures on an idle turn every five minutes, best-effort, so a gate closes when its item verifies on a later reading rather than when anybody says so. AN OLDER CONTROL PLANE answers the profile read 404, and the runner measures nothing.

A PERSONAL FLIGHT SAYS WHOSE MACHINES IT WAITS FOR. ADR-0024, slice forty-two rule 12. A personal watch's flight runs only on a machine its person has claimed (slice forty-three rule 10), so when none of theirs is asking for work it is offered to nobody - correctly, and silently, while every fleet surface reads healthy. `ReasonKinds.PersonalRunnerAbsent` (`personal-runner-absent`) is the sentence: params [person], a display, or [] when they have left the tenant, which the sentence says rather than leaving a hole. It is a wait, filed in the `failed` family with the three withholdings: the flight was admitted and runs the moment one of their machines asks. It is not `no-runner-advertises` (capacity is not what is missing) and not `runner-reserved` (a personal watch follows whose a machine is, not what it is kept for), so its remedy is to start or claim a machine of theirs - never to reserve one. AN OLDER gg shown this kind fails to render it, loudly and on purpose - an unknown kind poisons, never blanks - naming the kind it does not know rather than showing nothing; updating gg is the remedy.

A PROFILE SAYS WHICH RELAYS ITS MACHINES USE. Slice forty-three, found by the vmlinux002 walk (S43.8-01). `FleetProfile` gains `relays`, in `stun-servers`' spelling: the tenant's choice of where machines under it ask what they look like from outside. gg will not default one - the well-known public relays are run by companies this binary may not name, and a default would point every runner in every deployment at somebody's free service on a path carrying the shape of a customer's private network - so a pool member takes them from its strategy and an enrolled machine had nowhere to take them from at all. Measured: without relays the agent-login ceremony, which is the remedy a bring-up gate names, reached the runner and ended in "no route between them was found", so the machine could not answer its own ask and somebody set a machine setting by hand. `FleetProfile.IsRelay` is the shared question - a scheme is required, never assumed - and the machine's own reader now asks it rather than keeping a second copy; the two still differ in what they do with a bad entry, this refusing the document and that dropping the line. ADDING A RELAY IS NOT A WIDENING, which is the offer rule's decision rather than a new one: `stun-servers` is in `OfferableKeys.Unwatched`, because a wrong relay degrades a connection while a wrong forge host fetches code from somewhere nobody chose. AN OLDER CONTROL PLANE never offers the key, and an older gg reading a profile that carries relays refuses the document by its closed key set - which is the key set working.

A BOARD ROW SAYS WHOSE IT IS. ADR-0024, slice forty-two rules 13 and 14. A personal watch's rows stand on the tenant's board - one board - and only their person may decide them, so a listing that does not say whose a row is hides the one line a reader can act on, and the 403 for answering somebody else's arrives with no warning. `NominationSummary` gains `For`, a person's subject, and `ForDisplay`, their display while they are still in the tenant. BOTH, because a subject is opaque and names nobody a reader recognises, while a display alone cannot tell two people with one name apart and is dropped when somebody leaves - `gg board` prints the display first and the subject beside it, and prints NEITHER for a tenant row, which belongs to nobody and says so by saying nothing, as the topology read already does. AN OLDER CONTROL PLANE sends neither member, and every row then reads as the tenant's - which is what every row was before this.

A SWEEP SAYS AS WHOM IT READ. ADR-0024, slice forty-two rules 16 and 17. A sweep reads a tracker with a credential the SWEEPING MACHINE holds - the control plane holds a reference and resolves none - so only that machine can say what the credential acts as, and until now 'swept, 3 nominated' read the same whether it swept as a service account nobody minds or as a person whose queue it emptied. A GG_INTENT_HOSTS entry may now carry a third field, key=host|locator|account, and WatchAttestation gains Account, the account of the pair the swept watch named. A FACT AND NEVER A SECRET: CredentialReference's own rule for the locator beside it - knowing the name of an account grants nothing. NOT PART OF THE MATCH: a watch pairs with a runner on its host and its credential, and comparing a third field would unpair every watch whose operator had not written one yet, with no sentence anywhere saying why. An entry that names no account attests none rather than guessing, which is every pair declared before this: two fields parse exactly as they did.

WHAT IS RECORDED ABOUT A PERSON IS READABLE BY ONE. Found on slice forty-two's walk, 2026-09-20: a personal watch swept on its person's machine, opened a flight only that machine could take, and attested the account its credential acts as - and none of it could be read back. `FlightStory` gains `For` and `ForDisplay`, whose flight it is: a personal watch's person, a tenant watch's steward, or whoever opened it by hand, which is what the flight already carries as its author. A flight nobody is answerable for carries neither, the board row's rule. `WatchStanding` gains `Account`, the account the newest sweep read as, because "swept, 1 nominated" reads the same whoever it read as. Both are facts and never secrets - knowing what an account is called, or how a directory names somebody, grants nothing. AN OLDER CONTROL PLANE sends none of the three, and every read then says what it said before: nothing about whose work it was.

A BRING-UP GATE SAYS WHAT IS MISSING. Slice forty-six, step 4, and the kind the control plane has been waiting for: `AttemptLedger` refused to label a bring-up ask at all - "until the contract has a kind for it, a bring-up gate is an ordinary gate whose intent names the remedy" - because offering "sign the agent in" for a missing credential is the wrong act on the right machine. `GateMaintenanceKinds.BringUp` joins `AgentLogin`, and `GateMaintenance` gains `item` (one of `ReadinessKinds`: agent, credential, forge) and `subject` (what was checked - the agent's name, the credential's reference, the forge's key - never what a check produced). `provider` stops being required: a machine that cannot reach its forge has no provider in the sense that member means, and filling it with the forge's key would put one vocabulary's word in another's field; every agent-login gate still sets it, which is what its own act reads. AN OLDER gg renders an unknown kind as an ordinary gate rather than guessing an act for it, which is this vocabulary's stated rule and unchanged - so a bring-up gate on an older console reads as the gate it always was, with its remedy in the intent.

THE FLEET SAYS WHAT A MACHINE LACKS. Slice forty-six, step 5. `RunnerSummary` gains `lacks` - the UNMET items of a machine's most recent readiness reading, in `ReadinessItem`'s own shape so one vocabulary describes a reading whichever direction it travels - and `readinessMeasuredAt`. On the fleet read rather than behind a second call: a console draws the fleet in one request and a person scanning it is asking which machines are not working, so a round trip per row is the thing this avoids. SILENCE IS NOT HEALTH, which is why the instant is beside the list: a machine that has never measured itself carries an empty list exactly as one that meets everything does, and a console that read empty as ready would call an unmeasured machine fine. AN OLDER CONTROL PLANE sends neither, which reads as a fleet that has never measured itself - true of it, and the honest answer.
